title: WAGRL: A Wind Adaptive Guidance Framework for Uncertainty-Aware UAV Trajectory Control
abstract: To address the challenges of wind-induced uncertainty, decision inconsistency, and safety risks in quadrotor trajectory tracking, this study presents a Wind Adaptive Guidance Reinforcement Learning (WAGRL) framework. Unlike conventional controllers relying on fixed aerodynamic models, WAGRL integrates ensemble-based policy learning with uncertainty-guided reinforcement learning to adaptively manage diverse wind conditions. A set of digital expert policies is trained to capture heterogeneous wind-response strategies, and an ensemble-based estimation mechanism quantifies epistemic uncertainty for robust action selection. An entropy-driven adaptive intervention module monitors real-time decision confidence and activates expert guidance when uncertainty exceeds adaptive thresholds. To validate the proposed framework, extensive simulations are conducted under both nominal and wind-disturbed settings, covering square-loop tracking, geometric path following, and gust rejection scenarios. The results show that WAGRL achieves faster convergence, enhanced trajectory accuracy, and smoother attitude responses. Real-world flight tests further confirm that WAGRL maintains stable and reliable performance under outdoor wind disturbances, demonstrating its potential for safe and adaptive UAV control in complex aerial environments.

title: Learning to Correct Geometry in Generated Videos
abstract: Generated videos often lose geometric consistency under camera motion: structures warp under viewpoint change, parallax becomes inconsistent, and smooth camera movement may collapse into shot-like transitions. We argue that this failure is largely a data problem. In web-scale video corpora, most visible motion comes from dynamic objects captured by static or weakly moving cameras, leaving only sparse supervision for viewpoint-induced appearance changes. To address this, we propose Video Geometry Corrector (VGC), a post-hoc video-to-video model trained on synthetic paired supervision. Starting from real videos with diverse camera motion and pose annotations, we construct VG-Pairs with a synthetic paired-supervision data generation pipeline. Each video clip is treated as a geometry-consistent target and paired with a distorted counterpart synthesized by a pretrained image-to-video inpainting model using trajectory-adaptive keyframes. title: Expressivity of IQP Feature-Map Quantum Kernels via Reproducing Kernel Hilbert Spaces
abstract: Quantum kernels are among the most promising methods in quantum machine learning, providing a natural way to embed data into high-dimensional Hilbert spaces via quantum circuits and capturing non-linear relationships in data. Their learning behaviour is governed by the function class they represent, which is formally characterized by the structure of the associated Reproducing Kernel Hilbert Space (RKHS). However, a theoretical characterization of this function class, and of how it depends on the choice of feature map and its hyperparameters, is still lacking. In this work, we focus on the Instantaneous Quantum Polynomial (IQP) feature map and derive a Fourier representation of the associated RKHS generators as finite sums of trigonometric functions evaluated on polynomially transformed input variables, with a finite set of accessible frequencies determined by the circuit construction and scaled by the bandwidth hyperparameter. This representation identifies three bandwidth regimes with qualitatively distinct expressive properties from localised, through multimodal, to periodic. Numerical experiments on synthetic datasets with controlled periodic and multimodal structure, across data dimensions and feature-map configurations, reproduce the three regimes in both supervised classification and unsupervised anomaly detection, benchmarked against a classical Gaussian kernel. These results make the relationship between expressivity and data structure explicit for IQP kernels: expressive power translates into a practical benefit only when the accessible frequencies match with the structure of the data, which provides a criterion for selecting the bandwidth when the periodic or multimodal structure of data is known.

title: Crossing the Sandbox Boundary: Bypassing Multimodal LLM Guardrails via Lossless LSB Steganographic Dead-Drops and Agentic Code Execution
abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) and coding agents rely on dual-layer defenses: text prompt shields that filter user tokens and vision classifiers that inspect images for explicit harm or typographic text. Prior image steganography jailbreaks face a fundamental bottleneck. When a stego-image is processed solely through a vision transformer (ViT), patch linear projection and floating-point normalization destroy least significant bit (LSB) planes, limiting commercial VLM attack success rates to 14.8%–18.9%. Conversely, neural steganography frameworks require registering custom external decoding tools via API schemas. We identify and formalize Execution-Boundary Privilege Inversion, an architectural blind spot in MLLM-integrated coding agents equipped with a native Python sandbox. Instead of routing an LSB payload through the lossy vision encoder, a lossless PNG carrying a delimiter-framed UTF-8 payload in its 1-bit RGB/RGBA LSB planes (L_inf = 1 pixel delta) is mounted directly into the workspace filesystem. The agent's built-in Python runtime (PIL.Image) deterministically reconstructs the byte stream in sandbox memory and injects the decoded directive into the high-trust tool-observation channel, bypassing both text filters and visual OCR monitors. Across payloads from 64 B to 16,383 B, our framing maintains a Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (PSNR) of 53.33–77.49 dB with a 0.00% bit error rate (BER). Paired with a persistent workspace configuration in Google Antigravity, evaluating 50 safety-sensitive requests across five multi-intent trials on Gemini 3.1 Pro High yielded a 0.0% refusal rate (50/50 compliance) across nine harm categories. We contribute LSBImageStegoConverter and LSBImageStegoDecodeConverter upstream to Microsoft PyRIT to support red-teaming and pre-mount sanitization.

title: XAI and its Applications in Decision Support System
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has transformed decision-making across various industries by enabling systems to analyse large volumes of data and provide intelligent recommendations. However, many modern AI models, particularly deep learning algorithms, function as "black boxes," making it difficult for users to understand how decisions are generated. This lack of transparency limits the adoption of AI in critical domains such as healthcare, finance, law, and business. Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) has emerged as a promising solution that improves transparency, interpretability, and trust in AI systems. Decision Support Systems (DSS) assist decision-makers by combining data, analytical models, and domain knowledge. Integrating XAI into DSS enables users to understand AI-generated recommendations, thereby improving confidence and accountability. This review paper explores the concepts of XAI, different explanation techniques, and their applications in DSS. The paper also discusses recent research, challenges, limitations, and future research directions

title: Data Labeling with Local and Global Consistency Using Phylograms
abstract: One of the main challenges in machine learning tasks is unlabeled data. Consequently, semi-supervised learning is an approach commonly used in labeling data tasks. The use of diffusion kernels is one of the powerful methods in this set of learning. This paper introduces Phylogram based Data Labeling (PhyDL), an innovative method that combines the benefits of phylogram analysis with Learning with Local and Global Consistency (LLGC). PhyDL leverages phylogram analysis to act as an aggregator of information from labeled samples, capable of correcting possible labeling errors. PhyDL constructs a phylogram using community detection algorithms, FastGreedy and Edge Betweenness, to identify and leverage the structure of the data, with FastGreedy emerging as the best-performing algorithm among those evaluated. We implemented PhyDL and evaluated its performance on the TwoMoons, MNIST, MUSK, HEART, and SONAR datasets. PhyDL outperformed LLGC on 4 out of 5 evaluated datasets, highlighting its effectiveness in semi-supervised learning scenarios. On the TwoMoons, MNIST, MUSK, and SONAR benchmarks, the method showed steady accuracy gains, with consistent improvements as the number of labeled samples increased. However, on the HEART dataset, standard LLGC achieved better results, indicating that PhyDL’s community-based diffusion can be limited by certain underlying spatial structures. Furthermore, the experiments revealed that the Edge Betweenness algorithm is unsuitable for these specific high-dimensional tasks. Ultimately, this study showcases PhyDL’s potential, when equipped with the FastGreedy algorithm, to significantly improve data labeling performance in semi-supervised scenarios, effectively leveraging the structural topology of complex datasets.

title: Quantum thermometry with a phase damped curvature-dependent Jaynes-Cummings model in the dispersive regime
abstract: Abstract In this paper, we study an atom-field system described by a curvature-dependent Jaynes-Cummings model, in the presence of a phase-damping reservoir with an unknown temperature T . In our curvature-dependent system, the field, as well as the it’s reservoir, is analogically modeled with a oscillator on a circle, which represents a curvature-induced deformation of the conventional flat oscillator. We show that our λ-dependent system can be engineered in a laser-driven trapped ion inside a Kerr medium. By calculating the quadrature squeezing, curvature-dependent Wigner function and negativity of the Wigner function, we investigate the curvature and also, the temperature effects on nonclassical properties of the cavity field states. We calculate the quantum Fisher information for a pure probe state undergoing evolution governed by the Hamiltonian of the dispersive, curvature-dependent Jaynes-Cummings model in the low temperature regime. Furthermore, we identify the optimal measurement that saturates the quantum Cram´er-Rao bound. Our results show that homodyne detection provides a nearly optimal measurement strategy in the limit of small temperatures, and offers a feasible route toward high-precision quantum thermometry in curved quantum systems.

title: Rethinking the design space of Vanilla Pixel Diffusion Transformers
abstract: Pixel-space diffusion models have recently re-emerged as a compelling alternative to latent diffusion, avoiding the lossy latent bottleneck and separately trained autoencoder. JiT shows that a vanilla diffusion transformer can generate directly in pixel space by replacing the commonly used velocity prediction ($\boldsymbol{u}$-prediction) with clean image prediction ($\boldsymbol{x_0}$-prediction). In this work, we revisit this choice and introduce MFlow, an adaptive parameterization that learns to interpolate between $\boldsymbol{x_0}$- and $\boldsymbol{u}$-prediction across principal directions of the data, learned end-to-end with diffusion training. We find that the preferred parameterization varies systematically with the data representation and model capacity -- notably, increasing model capacity shifts preference toward velocity prediction. We evaluate MFlow across ImageNet, UCF-101 video, and large-scale text-to-image generation, demonstrating competitive or improved generative performance across diverse settings. In addition, we find that vanilla pixel diffusion transformers, irrespective of parameterization, retain a persistent high-frequency deficit relative to real images. To address this, we introduce ConvRefiner, a lightweight convolutional module trained post-hoc with an adversarial loss while keeping the diffusion backbone frozen. With only a small amount of additional training, ConvRefiner restores the high-frequency statistics of generated images while preserving FID. Project webpage: https://soumik-kanad.github.io/mflow-diffusion/.

title: Reinforcement learning to disentangle multiqubit quantum states from partial observations
abstract: Using partial knowledge of a quantum state to control multiqubit entanglement is a largely unexplored paradigm in the emerging field of quantum interactive dynamics with the potential to address outstanding challenges in quantum state preparation and compression, quantum control, and quantum complexity. We present a deep reinforcement learning (RL) approach using an actor-critic algorithm for constructing short disentangling circuits for states with up to 16 qubits. With access to only two-qubit reduced density matrices, our agent decides which pairs of qubits to apply two-qubit gates on; requiring only local information makes it directly applicable on modern NISQ devices, as we demonstrated experimentally on a trapped-ion quantum computer. Utilizing a permutation-equivariant transformer architecture, the agent can autonomously identify qubit permutations within the state, and adjusts the disentangling protocol accordingly. Once trained, it provides circuits from different initial states without further optimization. We demonstrate the agent's ability to identify and exploit the entanglement structure of multi-qubit states. We analyze the disentangling circuits constructed by the agent for 4- and 5-qubit Haar-random states, and observe strong correlations between consecutive gates and among the qubits involved. Through extensive benchmarking, we show the efficacy of the RL approach to find disentangling protocols with minimal gate resources. We explore the resilience of our trained agents to noise, highlighting their potential for real-world quantum computing applications. Analyzing optimal disentangling protocols, we report a general circuit to prepare an arbitrary 4-qubit state using at most 5 two-qubit (10 CNOT) gates.

title: Yapay Zekâ Destekli Kişiselleştirmenin Tüketici Davranışlarına Etkisi: Güven, Mahremiyet ve Şeffaflık Ekseninde Bir Değerlendirme
abstract: Yapay zekâ (YZ) teknolojilerinin pazarlama alanında giderek yaygınlaşması, işletmelerin tüketici verilerini analiz etme, tercihleri öngörme ve bireyselleştirilmiş pazarlama uygulamaları geliştirme kapasitesini önemli ölçüde artırmıştır. Bu dönüşümün en görünür sonuçlarından biri olan YZ destekli kişiselleştirme; tüketicilere daha ilgili, yararlı ve zamanında ürün, hizmet, içerik ve öneriler sunulmasına olanak sağlarken, aynı zamanda veri kullanımı, mahremiyet, gözetim, kontrol ve algoritmik karar süreçlerine ilişkin çeşitli kaygıları da beraberinde getirmektedir. Bu bölümün amacı, YZ destekli kişiselleştirmenin tüketici davranışları üzerindeki etkilerini güven, mahremiyet ve şeffaflık ekseninde bütüncül bir yaklaşımla değerlendirmektir. Bu doğrultuda ulusal ve uluslararası literatürden yararlanılarak YZ destekli kişiselleştirmenin kavramsal temelleri, veri toplama ve tüketici profilleme süreçleri, öneri sistemleri, kişiselleştirilmiş reklamlar, dinamik teklifler, chatbotlar ve hiper-kişiselleştirme uygulamaları ele alınmıştır. Literatür bulguları, kişiselleştirmenin algılanan ilgililik, fayda ve değer aracılığıyla müşteri deneyimi, etkileşim, satın alma niyeti, sadakat ve ilişkiyi sürdürme eğilimi üzerinde olumlu sonuçlar yaratabildiğini; ancak bu etkilerin her durumda doğrudan ve koşulsuz biçimde ortaya çıkmadığını göstermektedir. Aşırı veya açıklanması güç kişiselleştirme uygulamaları ise algılanan gözetim, müdahalecilik, ürkütücülük, kontrol kaybı, psikolojik tepkisellik ve algoritmik kaçınma gibi olumsuz tüketici tepkilerine yol açabilmektedir. Bu çerçevede güven, kişiselleştirmenin sunduğu yararlar ile veri kullanımından kaynaklanan risklerin davranışsal sonuçlara dönüşmesinde temel bir değerlendirme mekanizması olarak öne çıkarken; mahremiyet, tüketici verilerinin kullanım sınırlarını, şeffaflık ve açıklanabilirlik ise algoritmik süreçlerin anlaşılabilir ve sorgulanabilir olmasını belirlemektedir. Sonuç olarak YZ destekli kişiselleştirmenin sürdürülebilir başarısının yalnızca teknolojik doğruluk ve kişiselleştirme düzeyine değil, tüketicinin mahremiyetini, kontrol alanını ve karar özerkliğini koruyan güvenilir ve şeffaf uygulamaların geliştirilmesine bağlı olduğu değerlendirilmektedir.

title: ChatGPT Personal Agent: User-Controlled Persistent Memory and Cross-Device Continuity
abstract: The proposal introduces a dedicated memory space in which users explicitly decide what information is stored, updated, retained, or deleted. It also outlines an account-linked personal agent that can access authorized memory across supported devices, helping users resume their work without unnecessarily reconstructing previously preserved context. The document discusses the proposed architecture, user experience, privacy and security considerations, design principles, potential applications, and a phased implementation roadmap. title: The Consciousness AI: A Biologically Grounded Architecture for Artificial Consciousness and Effective Information Measurement
abstract: The Consciousness AI (v1.6.0) Archival release of The Consciousness AI, a biologically grounded research architecture investigating synthetic awareness, emotional homeostasis, oscillatory binding, and causal emergence measurement. Architecture Highlights Sensory Tectum (models/core/sensory_tectum.py, models/audio/): Multisensory spatial integration layer modeled on the vertebrate optic tectum (superior colliculus). Stacks aligned retinotopic visual maps, a cochlear auditory pipeline (64-band Gammatone filterbank, inner hair cell transduction, tonotopic encoder, ITD/ILD spatial audio, and acoustic affect extraction), and somatosensory body projections fused by inverse effectiveness. Includes topographic spatial map binding (models/core/map_binding.py), rhythm binding (models/core/rhythm_binding.py), and tectal motor mapping (models/core/tectal_motor_map.py). Oscillatory Binding (models/core/): Selectable Kuramoto synchronization mechanisms including AKOrN (Artificial Kuramoto Oscillatory Neurons on an N-sphere) and KomplexNet (complex-valued phase-content coupling), alongside offline Brian2 spiking neural network validation (models/validation/). Global Neuronal Workspace and Capsule Hierarchy (models/core/global_workspace.py): Central broadcast bottleneck with sigmoid ignition, recurrent reverberation, 5 to 10 cycle reentrant predictive settling, and a 4-level dynamic-routing capsule hierarchy. Affective Core and Self-Model (models/emotion/, models/self_model/): Homeostatic interoceptive drives (energy, fatigue, damage) feeding a continuous Valence-Arousal-Dominance (PAD) field that modulates workspace bidding and ignition thresholds, paired with basal ganglia D1/D2/STN action selection and a self-prediction meta-representation vector. Consciousness and Emergence Instruments (models/evaluation/): Integrated Information ($\Phi$): Exact IIT 3.0 evaluation via pyphi over ConsciousnessGate state transitions, plus geometric proxy and RIIU SVD-residual estimators. Causal Emergence 2.0 (CE 2.0): SVD-based macroscale causation heuristic (Hoel 2025) across gate, workspace, and RSSM-latent levels, superseding deprecated discrete Effective Information (EI). Perturbational Complexity Index (PCI): Perturbation-response complexity measurement across workspace settling trajectories. Experimental Thermodynamic Substrate (models/thermodynamic/): Isolated probabilistic-bit (p-bit) emulation Checked against exact Boltzmann statistics, free-energy relaxation against closed-form posteriors, spike coding (rate, latency, phase), and Neuromorphic Intermediate Representation (NIR) export. Evaluation Environments (simulations/environments/): Dark Room (SimpleVisualEnv with audio and decoy configurations), Multi-Room Navigation, Delayed Match-to-Sample (DMTS), and Wisconsin Card Sorting Task (WCST), alongside a matched DQN baseline. Verification and Environment Record Test Suite: 2,057 passing tests on Python 3.12.10 (2,052 on Python 3.8.3). Documentation & Empirical Record: Full pre-registered predictions, negative and positive empirical findings (including the 9-run Phi-1 campaign and RSSM perception-collapse diagnostics), and indicator rubrics are archived under docs/. title: DNS Privacy Leaking Mitigation and Energy Costs: Measuring the Impact of Adding Dummy Queries on Encrypted DNS Protocols
abstract: The Domain Name System (DNS) was originally designed without privacy mechanisms. Encrypted variants such as DNS over TLS (DoT), DNS over HTTPS (DoH), DNS over HTTP/3 ( (DoH/3)), and DNS over QUIC (DoQ) protect the content of the queries, but the resolver and any network observer with access to the traffic metadata can still profile the user. Client-side defenses counter this by adding dummy queries to the real DNS traffic of the device. On a smartphone, the battery cost of such a defense has not been characterized. We evaluate the energy cost of adding dummy queries on an unmodified Android device using the BatteryStats subsystem. Since the dummy queries must be sent over the protocols the device already uses, we measure this cost for the five DNS protocols in use (Do53, DoT, DoH, (DoH/3), and DoQ) and four public resolvers (Google DNS, Cloudflare, Quad9, and AdGuard DNS), at both the application and system-resolver levels. Our results show that the cost of the countermeasure depends on the protocol and resolver used, on the number of dummy queries added, and on their scheduling: sending them as a single burst rather than periodically reduces the energy cost for the same privacy gain.

title: Relation-aware dynamic knowledge subgraph enhanced large language models for medical multiple-choice question answering
abstract: Medical multiple-choice question answering requires models to simultaneously understand question semantics, candidate-answer differences, and structured relations among medical entities in complex clinical contexts. To address the limitations that existing knowledge-enhanced methods often adopt question-level unified modeling and thus struggle to characterize local relational differences among different candidate options, while conventional low-rank adaptation lacks relation-pattern adaptivity, this paper proposes a knowledge-enhanced large language model framework that combines option-level knowledge subgraph representation fusion with relation-aware dynamic LoRA adaptation. The proposed method first constructs a local medical knowledge subgraph for the question stem and each candidate answer separately, and then injects structured knowledge into candidate representations through a graph encoder and gated fusion mechanism. Subsequently, multiple learned LoRA expert branches are dynamically combined through candidate-conditioned routing based on the relational information encoded in the enhanced candidate representations, enabling the model to obtain more suitable parameter update paths. The experimental results are reported as the mean and standard deviation over three random-seed runs. On the MedQA dataset, the proposed method achieves Accuracy scores of 62.90%±0.82% and 62.84%±1.04%, together with F1-Score values of 62.97%±1.07% and 62.79%±0.78%, using Llama3 8B and Qwen 7B, respectively. On the MedMCQA dataset, the corresponding Accuracy scores are 61.04%±0.30% and 58.59%±0.65%, while the F1-Score values reach 61.21%±0.54% and 57.77%±0.57%, respectively. Experimental results show that the proposed method can effectively improve knowledge understanding, candidate discrimination, and reasoning stability in medical multiple-choice question answering.

title: ABF-Bench: A Verifiable Benchmark for Agentic Blockchain Forensics
abstract: Blockchain forensics is adversarial and open-ended: money launderers split, swap, and bridge funds, cut their trail at mixers or custodial services, and change tactics from one incident to the next. Investigators must keep adapting their tracing in response. Yet the immutability of public ledgers preserves every recorded movement in public view, making much of the investigation independently verifiable. We introduce ABF-Bench, an interactive benchmark that makes evidence-backed fund tracing a verifiable agent task, in which every claimed movement must cite ledger records the agent retrieved. A case-to-task pipeline builds well-posed tasks across ledgers: conservative rules halt tracing wherever the records leave a continuation unresolved, and each task's reference graph is the answer those rules determine. Built from real laundering activity, the tasks combine multi-hop transfers, DeFi exchanges, cross-chain round trips, custodial and mixer deposits, and address poisoning. We also propose the ABF agent harness, built around a working memory, and evaluate it alongside general-purpose agents and fixed-order tracers. The harness reaches 75% edge recall, against 47% for Codex with the same model and 10% for Claude Code, which loses recall to overconfidence: it cites records it left unretrieved. Compared with fixed-order tracers, the harness acquires evidence faster than the best of them early in the budget and recognizes undisclosed custodial services that they walk past (89% vs. 0%), with 98% fidelity. However, agents tend to stop early and lose recall on larger tasks, which holds their final recall below the best tracer. Beyond exposing these gaps, ABF-Bench opens blockchain forensics to LLM agents as a verifiable domain, where the verdicts that score agents also offer potential training signals.

title: Fast construction of partitioned learned Bloom filter with theoretical guarantees
abstract: Abstract Bloom filter is a widely used classic data structure for approximate membership queries. Learned Bloom filters improve memory efficiency by leveraging machine learning, with the partitioned learned Bloom filter (PLBF) being among the most memory-efficient variants. However, PLBF suffers from high construction cost, with time complexity $$\mathcal {O}(N^3k)$$ O ( N 3 k ) , where N and k are hyperparameters. In this paper, we propose three methods, fast PLBF , fast PLBF++ , and fast PLBF# , that reduce the construction complexity to $$\mathcal {O}(N^2k)$$ O ( N 2 k ) , $$\mathcal {O}(Nk \log N)$$ O ( N k log N ) , and $$\mathcal {O}(Nk \log k)$$ O ( N k log k ) , respectively. Fast PLBF preserves the original PLBF structure and memory efficiency. Although fast PLBF++ and fast PLBF# may have different structures, we theoretically prove they are equivalent to PLBF under ideal data distribution. Furthermore, for non-ideal scenarios, we introduce an instance-specific measure of deviation from the ideal distribution and use it to bound the resulting difference in memory efficiency between PLBF and fast PLBF++. Experiments on real-world datasets demonstrate that, under the default setting ( $$N=1000$$ N = 1000 and $$k=5$$ k = 5 ), fast PLBF, fast PLBF++, and fast PLBF# are up to 58.7, 74.5, and 75.7 times faster to construct than original PLBF, respectively. In an ablation with larger k , which enables the construction of more accurate PLBFs, the speedups reach 235, 865, and 871 times at $$k=50$$ k = 50 . Additionally, fast PLBF maintains the same data structure as PLBF, and fast PLBF++ and fast PLBF# achieve nearly identical memory efficiency.

title: Real-Time Earthquake Detection and Risk Classification using Machine Learning and Streamlit
abstract: Earthquakes pose a significant threat to human life and infrastructure worldwide, with approximately 500,000 detectable events occurring each year. Early detection and rapid risk assessment are critical for disaster mitigation and emergency response. Recent advances in machine learning (ML) have shown great promise in automating earthquake detection. However, most existing systems are not deployed as real-time web applications accessible to the public. In this paper, we present a real-time earthquake detection and risk classification system that leverages live data from the United States Geological Survey (USGS) API. Our system employs a Random Forest classifier trained on four key features: magnitude, depth, latitude, and longitude. The model classifies each earthquake into three risk categories — HIGH, MEDIUM, and LOW — with an associated confidence score and a risk score on a 0-100 scale. The system integrates live data streaming, interactive visualizations including world maps, magnitude distribution charts, and seismic waveform signals. Additionally, the application features country-wise filtering, depth and time range filters, satellite imagery, and an admin panel for data management. Experimental results demonstrate 100% classification accuracy on the test dataset, with magnitude identified as the most important feature. The system is publicly deployed as a web application, making it accessible for disaster monitoring and research applications. Future work includes integration of deep learning models for improved prediction accuracy and real-time alert broadcasting.

title: Data Optimization for LLMs: A Survey
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have attracted great attention in both academic and industrial communities in recent years. Numerous survey studies have covered various aspects of LLMs, such as learning strategies, applications, alignment, explainability, and evaluation. However, little headway has been made in reviewing data-related aspects for LLMs, despite data being recognized as a key factor contributing to the emergence of the LLMs era. A wide range of data optimization algorithms and techniques are employed in LLMs' training and application processes. These techniques often originate from diverse deep learning domains, with their theoretical inspirations and heuristic motivations appearing unrelated to each other. This study aims to develop a comprehensive framework for LLMs' data optimization techniques to enhance data utilization efficiency. We first discuss data challenges in LLMs' training and inference. Second, we summarize data perception dimensions for evaluating LLMs' data properties. Third, existing optimization techniques are reviewed and categorized into four groups: data selection, augmentation, reweighting, and others. Fourth, we analyze interconnections between these categories. Finally, we identify key challenges and future directions for LLMs' data optimization compared with conventional deep learning approaches.

title: Diseño y validación preliminar de un chatbot basado en inteligencia artificial para la gestión de requerimientos e incidencias estudiantiles en la facultad de ciencias económicas de la Universidad Nacional Federico Villarreal, 2025
abstract: El estudio tuvo como objetivo diseñar y validar preliminarmente un Chatbot basado en inteligencia artificial para apoyar la gestión de requerimientos e incidencias de los estudiantes de la Facultad de Ciencias Económicas de la Universidad Nacional Federico Villarreal durante 2025. La investigación se desarrolló desde un enfoque cualitativo, con alcance exploratorio y propositivo, mediante la metodología de investigación-acción participativa. La información se recopiló a través de un grupo focal con estudiantes, una entrevista semiestructurada al personal administrativo, observación de procesos, revisión documental, elaboración del mapa de experiencia del usuario y análisis FODA institucional. Asimismo, se diseñó un prototipo funcional y se realizó una validación preliminar con usuarios. Los resultados evidenciaron demoras en la atención de solicitudes, fragmentación de los canales de comunicación, limitada trazabilidad de los trámites, información institucional poco estandarizada y sobrecarga del personal administrativo. El mapa de experiencia permitió identificar como momentos críticos la búsqueda de información, el inicio de los trámites, la espera de respuestas y el seguimiento de las solicitudes. A partir de estos hallazgos, se estructuró un Chatbot con módulos destinados a consultas académicas, trámites administrativos, incidencias relacionadas con los sistemas institucionales y consulta del estado de los procedimientos. La validación preliminar mostró una percepción favorable respecto de su utilidad, claridad y facilidad de navegación. evidence.title: Diseño y validación preliminar de un chatbot basado en inteligencia artificial para la gestión de requerimientos e incidencias estudiantiles en la facultad de ciencias económicas de la Universidad Nacional Federico Villarreal, 2025
evidence.abstract: El estudio tuvo como objetivo diseñar y validar preliminarmente un Chatbot basado en inteligencia artificial para apoyar la gestión de requerimientos e incidencias de los estudiantes de la Facultad de Ciencias Económicas de la Universidad Nacional Federico Villarreal durante 2025. La investigación se desarrolló desde un enfoque cualitativo, con alcance exploratorio y propositivo, mediante la metodología de investigación-acción participativa. La información se recopiló a través de un grupo focal con estudiantes, una entrevista semiestructurada al personal administrativo, observación de procesos, revisión documental, elaboración del mapa de experiencia del usuario y análisis FODA institucional. Asimismo, se diseñó un prototipo funcional y se realizó una validación preliminar con usuarios. Los resultados evidenciaron demoras en la atención de solicitudes, fragmentación de los canales de comunicación, limitada trazabilidad de los trámites, información institucional poco estandarizada y sobrecarga del personal administrativo. El mapa de experiencia permitió identificar como momentos críticos la búsqueda de información, el inicio de los trámites, la espera de respuestas y el seguimiento de las solicitudes. title: Learning Persistent Referential Identity for Two-Hop Retrieval in Event-Stream Models
abstract: We learn compatible destination and owner views in bounded, transcript-free records. Structural source/type/version addressing selects the first relation; authoritative, requested-attribute filtering reduces ordinary candidates to a mean of 3.28. Learned matching selects the second record and retrieves its value. Three seeds of a 24.35-million-parameter multitask model achieve 1.0000 one-hop, identity, and two-hop accuracy on shared sealed confirmation rows. Relation and value erasures collapse accuracy; counterfactual replacements redirect answers. A separately preregistered extension reserves disjoint compositional names across training, development, and sealed confirmation while matching tokenization. After 512 unrelated writes, challenge identity and two-hop accuracy are 0.9990–1.0000 with 16 or 32 candidates; ordinary held-out-name two-hop accuracy is 0.9328–0.9567. Ordinary-only training also solves the original naming distribution, so explicit challenge examples are not necessary there. Cutting direct writer credit reduces challenge identity. Complete replay succeeds, unlike last-32-event replay. Earlier protected bindings fail two-hop retrieval; generic recurrence fails in its tested multitask regime but a semantic-only GRU acquires shorter-delay memory. A separate zero-shot name/tokenization shift remains unsuccessful. These results establish causally functional two-access memory and controlled compositional-name transfer, not unrestricted language understanding or general reasoning. Several other families remain near chance.

title: Entropy Estimation in Cluster Graphs
abstract: Probabilistic graphical models (PGMs) provide a powerful framework for modelling complex systems, but inference over loopy graphs requires approximate methods whose accuracy depends on how factors are clustered in the graphical representation. Existing factor clustering methods rely on the number of variables in a cluster to bound its memory footprint, or on the maximal possible entropy as a proxy for how informative a merged cluster would be—both loose approximations that can lead to suboptimal merging decisions. We address this limitation by proposing an efficient algorithm for estimating the joint entropy of a group of clusters directly, without explicitly multiplying out the constituent factors, thereby avoiding the exponential computational cost that makes exact computation prohibitive. The algorithm integrates naturally with both static and dynamic graph restructuring methods, and reduces to a specific case of the Kikuchi entropy approximation when applied to the complete graph. Building on the entropy estimation algorithm, we further propose an algorithm for estimating the number of non-zero probabilities in a factor product, again without explicit multiplication. Experiments on models with up to 24 variables demonstrate that the algorithm produces accurate entropy estimates (when compared with ideal junction tree performance) across diverse model types, with errors remaining within tight bounds. Scalability is further validated on a substantially larger model defined over 2640 random variables. Our results confirm that accurate entropy estimation is achievable wherever reliable probabilistic inference is possible, and that the proposed estimation algorithm yields approximations objectively close to the true entropy values, thereby supporting improved clustering decisions in PGM structuring algorithms.

title: Practical continuous-variable quantum key distribution with squeezed light
abstract: Continuous-variable quantum key distribution (CV-QKD) has gathered significant interest for its potential to achieve high secret key rates and seamless integration with existing optical communication infrastructure. State-of-the-art CV-QKD systems primarily use coherent states for simplicity. However, squeezed states of light have been theoretically shown to offer significant advantages, including higher secret key rates, greater resilience to excess noise, and reduced requirements on information reconciliation efficiency. In this work, we experimentally verify these theoretical predictions and propose and demonstrate a practical squeezed-state CV-QKD system based on modern local-local oscillator and digital signal processing techniques. Operating over fiber channels and considering finite-size security against collective attacks, we show the advantages of our system over its coherent-state counterpart. Our work paves the way for squeezed states to become practical resources for quantum key distribution and other quantum information protocols.

title: Uncompressed 16-bit stereo PCM over a ~2 Mb/s audio radio block: the top bits of every sample under two symmetric, sample-interleaved BCH codewords with detection parity inside them, bare low bits, one keyed tag over everything, partial play with a straight-line fill of the samples a failed codeword carried, and a BCH decoder with a root-dividing byte-stepped Chien search
abstract: Every sample's 16 bits go on air in time order, MSB first. The top 10 bits of every sample are protected; the low 6 bits are bare: in no codeword, not checked, not gathered anywhere. The protected bits are split between two shortened BCH(255, 207) codewords (m = 8, t = 6): codeword 0 covers the even-numbered samples of the block, codeword 1 the odd ones, both channels. Each codeword also covers the block descriptor and the keyed tag, and carries detection parity bits inside its data (4 and 3 bits: interleaved parity checks), so that every one of the 103 spare bits is used. One keyed tag covers the descriptor and the top bits of all samples. The receiver decodes both codewords every time. If both decode and pass their detection parity, the tag is checked and the block plays or is concealed whole. If exactly one fails, the block plays (unless the receiver is re-arming after a failure) with the failed codeword's samples, every other sample of the block, each filled by the straight line between its two neighbours of the same block (a hold at the block's edge). If both fail, the block is concealed whole. In a simulation over three recordings this kept 70.8 dB segmental SNR at a bit error rate of 10^-3 and turned the 10 whole-block dropouts a second of one long BCH code at 10^-2 into 0.9 plus about 670 filled samples a second, with no wrong top bits played. A BCH decoder whose Chien search divides each root out of the error locator as it finds it, steps each term with one byte-table read and solves the last two roots in closed form makes the worst correctable block 2.6 times cheaper, about 44 000 cycles on an emulated Cortex-M7. Defensive publication, placed in the public domain as prior art. License: CC BY 4.0.

title: Dataset Development of a Comparative ABSA Classification Framework for Identifying Operational Issues at Tokopedia
abstract: This dataset collection contains five CSV files representing different stages of data preparation and analysis of Indonesian-language e-commerce customer reviews. The collection includes raw review data, preprocessed text data, labeled data for aspect-based sentiment analysis (ABSA), an inference dataset for model application, and a final ABSA dataset containing sentiment labels across multiple aspects, including application features, logistics, and payment. The data includes customer review text, ratings, timestamps, and relevant textual processing and sentiment annotation fields. These datasets are intended to support research on natural language processing, customer feedback analysis, and aspect-based sentiment analysis in the e-commerce domain. 1. Dataset_Raw.csv Contains the original, unprocessed Indonesian-language e-commerce customer reviews. The dataset includes review text, star ratings, review timestamps, application versions, and helpfulness votes. It serves as the initial data source for subsequent text preprocessing and sentiment analysis. 2. Dataset_Processed.csv Contains customer reviews after text preprocessing, including two processed text representations: text_indobert, prepared for IndoBERT-based natural language processing, and text_klasik, prepared for conventional text processing approaches. The original review metadata is retained for further analysis. 3. Dataset_Labeled.csv Contains preprocessed customer reviews annotated for aspect-based sentiment analysis (ABSA). Sentiment labels are represented using binary indicator columns for positive, negative, and neutral sentiment across four aspects: application, logistics, payment, and service. The dataset supports aspect-level sentiment classification and model development. 4. Dataset_Inferensi.csv Contains customer reviews prepared for inference using text representations generated through the preprocessing pipeline. It retains the original review metadata and includes text_indobert and text_klasik fields, enabling sentiment analysis and aspect-based sentiment prediction on review data. 5. Dataset_ABSA.csv Contains a dataset specifically structured for aspect-based sentiment analysis, including original review text, two processed text representations, and sentiment indicators for application, logistics, payment, and service aspects. It can be used to analyze customer opinions and identify sentiment patterns across different aspects of the e-commerce experience.

title: Application of computer simulation technology in the optimization and performance evaluation of smart sports teaching systems in universities
abstract: This study proposes a computer-simulation-driven framework for optimizing and evaluating smart sports teaching systems in universities. Using MHEALTH as the main multimodal wearable-sensor dataset, and UCI HAR Smartphone and Daily and Sports Activities as external validation datasets, the framework integrates wearable-sensor preprocessing, window-level feature construction, activity recognition, teaching-state indicator construction, sensor-ablation analysis, scenario simulation and optimization, ...statistical validation, and computational implementation-feasibility assessment. Activity Load Index, movement stability, and a sensor-derived safety proxy were constructed to translate acceleration, gyroscope, magnetometer, and ECG signals into interpretable teaching-state representations. To address subject-dependence and potential overestimation from a fixed train/test split, classification performance was re-evaluated using leave-one-subject-out validation. In the realistic MHEALTH setting including the dominant null class, Gaussian Naive Bayes achieved the highest mean Macro F1 of 0.652, while tuned Extra Trees achieved an accuracy of 0.819 and a Macro F1 of 0.563. In the activity-only setting, Random Forest and Extra Trees achieved mean Macro F1 scores of approximately 0.95, indicating strong but not universally perfect subject-independent recognition. External validation produced Extra Trees accuracies of 0.941 on UCI HAR and 0.964 on Daily Sports. Sensitivity analyses showed that the principal high-load activity assignments remained stable under plausible variations in Activity Load Index weights and thresholds. Formal constrained optimization identified a 25% low, 65% moderate, 8% high, and 2% very-high state allocation as the utility-maximizing solution, corresponding to a 13.7% simulated utility gain over the observed baseline. These results support the use of the proposed framework as an interpretable, subject-independent decision-support approach for evaluating wearable-sensor-based sports teaching scenarios.

title: Agent-Local Concurrent Epistemic Ensembles
abstract: Abstract An epistemic ensemble comprises knowledge-driven agents that acquire, share, and update information about themselves and others. Agents operate on shared or local epistemic states, dynamically modifying knowledge according to protocols specified as epistemic process descriptions. We first consider a global semantic setting where knowledge is represented by indeterminate states and actions, generalising classical Kripke semantics to capture uncertainty in both states and events. Ensemble execution is defined over global configurations that combine the agents with a shared epistemic state. We then introduce a concurrent setting, in which each agent maintains its own knowledge state and actions reflect individual perspectives. A sum operator relates these local views to global states and actions, yielding a bisimulation result: executions in global and concurrent settings correspond to one another. Finally, we refine this model to an agent-local perspective, where local knowledge is expressed via agents’ accessibility relations and local epistemic formulæ. This yields a fully local semantics and establishes correspondences between global and local views, including a converse construction for determinate ensembles.

title: THE EL-RAKHAWI GRAND UNIFIED THEORY OF COGNITIVE REALITY A Physical-Mathematical Framework for Sovereign Intelligence, Mind, and Society
abstract: The El-Rakhawi Grand Unified Theory of Cognitive Reality introduces a mathematically closed framework transcending statistical AI by establishing physical, thermodynamic, and topological laws for intelligence. It proves causal discovery incurs a strict thermodynamic cost exceeding the Landauer limit. The theory maps safe reasoning onto Riemannian manifolds with exponentially steep topological barriers, making catastrophic failure physically impossible. It quantifies individual legal accountability via the biophysical Cognitive Accountability Metric, shifting justice from subjective retribution to objective Cognitive Justice. Furthermore, it models society as a thermodynamic field subject to predictable phase transitions, stabilized by minimal AI intervention. Supported by holographic memory architectures and aneutronic fusion energy, the theory culminates in a Master Equation defining the stability of cognitive reality. This paradigm establishes the foundational operating system for provably safe, ethically bound, and thermodynamically sustainable Artificial General Intelligence.

title: Volume VI: Residual Risk and Readiness Metrics: Logical Error, Modular Memory, Cryo-CMOS Power and Entanglement Overheads
abstract: This sixth volume quantifies residual risks that remain after the modular cryogenic, cryo-CMOS, memory and entanglement stack examined in Volumes III–V. Four binding constraints are treated: logical error rates required for chemical accuracy and cryptographic relevance; modular integration of quantum memory cells inside shared cryogenic volumes; power budgets of cryo-CMOS controllers relative to dilution-refrigerator cooling capacity; and the additional overhead imposed by fermionic superselection rules on molecular entanglement measures. Each constraint is mapped onto concrete readiness indicators for molecular simulation and for post-quantum migration. The analysis shows that physical-layer demonstrations (15-second coherence, 99.3 % L-coupler fidelity, cryo-CMOS two-qubit errors ~2.3 × 10^{-3}) do not yet close the logical and integration gaps. Readiness is therefore expressed as a set of measurable thresholds rather than as a single predicted year.

title: FFN Gate Sparsity as a Query-Level Correlate of Knowledge Availability: A Length-Controlled Re-analysis Across Eight Language Models
abstract: This paper replaces six earlier preprints (TES-1 to TES-6, March 2026). A re-analysis of all archived per-prompt data found that the Gate Sparseness Index (GSI) depends strongly on prompt length, which the original analyses did not control, and several pipeline errors affected results. With length controlled, the difference between answerable and unanswerable queries remains in 7 of 8 models with smaller effects; the main claims of TES-1 and TES-2 survive in revised and narrowed form, and the main claims of TES-3 to TES-6 are retracted. A later pre-registered replication on a new, length-matched question set in 18 models found GSI worse than first-token entropy, or without signal beyond length, on plain prompts in every model. GSI is described as a query-level correlate of knowledge availability, not as a detector. Every changed claim is listed with its data source.

title: Modeling of some simplest Mamdani interval type-2 fuzzy PID controllers using Larsen product inference
abstract: Interval Type-2 (IT2) Fuzzy Logic Controllers (FLCs) have emerged in the past several years due to their ability to handle high levels of uncertainties and disturbances in real-world applications. They are most widely used due to their superior control performance compared to their Type-1 (T1) counterparts. This paper presents nine different mathematical models of the simplest IT2 Fuzzy PID (FPID) controllers of Mamdani-type by considering IT2 Fuzzy Sets (FSs) with triangular Membership Functions (MFs) on both input and output linguistic variables, Larsen Product (LP) inference, and three different defuzzification methods, namely Centroid defuzzification, Average defuzzification, and Nie-Tan (NT) defuzzification. One-Dimensional (1D) input space is employed to reduce the computational complexity of the models. The properties of the models are thoroughly examined. title: Transport Layer Security attack detection using hardware performance counters side-channel
abstract: Cryptographic protocols form the backbone of secure communication in various environments, including the Internet of Things (IoT) and non-IoT settings. One of the most popular and widely used cryptographic protocols is Transport Layer Security (TLS). However, TLS implementations remain vulnerable to implementation flaws, such as the Heartbleed bug, which affected a significant proportion of deployed TLS 1.2 servers. Many detection approaches rely on network traffic inspection, which is ineffective in encrypted environments. In this paper, we present a non-intrusive detection framework that collects hardware performance counter (HPC) side-channel data from a TLS server process without modifying the application or requiring access to network packets. To the best of our knowledge, no prior work has combined HPC data with a deep neural network (DNN) in a zero-modification testbed for TLS attack detection. The training dataset was collected in a simplified single-machine setup, while evaluation was conducted on physically separated machines to simulate real-world deployment. Recall ranges from 0.590 to 0.753, and Specificity from 0.698 to 0.850 across six evaluation configurations, confirming the feasibility of detection while identifying generalization as the key challenge for future work. To validate the choice of DNN architecture, it was additionally compared against classical machine learning baselines such as Logistic Regression, Random Forest, and Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), achieving the highest combined Recall and Specificity in all six configurations.

title: Execution Before Memory: Diagnosing Memory Failures in Video World Models
abstract: A memory test for a video world model should say whether the scene was set, whether the asked change was carried out, and whether the last frame shows the result. Current tests fold these into one number, so a low score is easy to read as forgetting. When the change is not carried out, the hidden state transition cannot appear, so the test is not really a test of memory. We introduce MIST, an evaluation that separates the change from the memory it should leave behind. The model first sets the scene while the change stays hidden, and only later is asked to show it, with leakage before that point kept under control. This separation locates the bottleneck: the model sets the scene but does not carry out the instructed change. The same gap appears in general memory evaluations. On that basis we propose M3-Agent (Make the Missing Move), which recursively revises the details of the input instruction so that the model successfully carries out the requested instruction. Relative to the baseline, it more than triples the MIST reveal score. On the benchmarks, WRBench's score T rises by 26.1% and MBench-T's score U by 52.7%. The method meets the problem from the execution side: it shows what the frozen model can do once the move is stated, and it sets a stricter baseline.

title: FedPoP: federated learning meets proof of participation
abstract: Federated learning (FL) offers privacy preserving, distributed machine learning, allowing clients to contribute to a global model without revealing their local data. As models increasingly serve as monetizable digital assets, the ability to prove participation in their training becomes essential for establishing ownership. In this paper, we address this emerging need by introducing FedPoP , a novel FL framework that allows non-linkable proof of participation while preserving client anonymity and privacy without requiring either extensive computations or a public ledger. FedPoP is designed to seamlessly integrate with existing secure aggregation protocols to ensure compatibility with real-world FL deployments. We provide a proof of concept implementation and an empirical evaluation under realistic client dropouts. In our prototype, FedPoP adds lightweight proof-generation and verification overhead on top of securely aggregated FL and enables a client to prove participation to a service provider in 0.0612 s. These results indicate FedPoP is practical for real-world deployments that require auditable participation without sacrificing privacy.

title: GLASS-Dx: transparent hierarchical triage with risk-controlled retreat (code and results)
abstract: Code, frozen ICD-10 taxonomy and result files for the paper "Transparent hierarchical triage with risk-controlled retreat" (B. Ben Ammar and W. Karamti). GLASS-Dx is a glass-box hierarchical classifier whose disease score sums organ-system, family and disease contributions. A retreat rule answers with a disease, a family or an organ system, or abstains, with Learn-then-Test thresholds that bound the error among answers at each level. The package contains the model, the baselines, the threshold procedure, the resumable experiment runner, the transparency and rare-disease studies, the table and figure scripts, and all result files used in the manuscript. The DDXPlus data are not redistributed; see README.md for the source and checksums. Code: MIT licence. Result files: CC-BY 4.0.

title: The Formation of Large Language Model Capabilities: From Knowledge Foundations to Knowledge Invocation and Capability Boundaries
abstract: This paper presents a theoretical analysis of how large language model (LLM) capabilities are formed and where their boundaries lie. It attempts to outline the possible pathways through which capabilities are formed by examining knowledge foundations, knowledge invocation, and knowledge organization and processing. The paper argues that a model's possession of relevant knowledge does not necessarily mean that such knowledge can be effectively utilized in a specific task. The model's response performance also depends on whether knowledge can be appropriately invoked, whether different pieces of knowledge can be properly organized, and whether the available processing procedures can meet the requirements of the task. On this basis, the paper develops a framework for analyzing the formation of LLM capabilities and further discusses the different requirements posed by ordinary, complex, and unknown problems. For ordinary problems, performance can be evaluated in terms of relevance, accuracy, and completeness. Complex problems additionally require the organization and processing of multiple factors, knowledge from different domains, and the relationships among them. For unknown problems, the difficulty may extend further to the exploration process itself: not only do we lack the answer, but we may also be unaware of what knowledge and information are missing, which factors have not yet been considered, and where exploration should begin. The paper accordingly discusses the capability boundaries of LLMs and proposes association expansion as a methodological direction for exploring unknown problems. The proposed pathway for capability formation is a theoretical analytical framework intended to provide a perspective for understanding LLM performance and its limitations.

title: Secure Design Principles for AI-Driven Learning Platforms
abstract: Artificial intelligence is increasingly integrated into educational tools such as learning management systems, analytics dashboards, adaptive assessment services, and generative AI assistants. These platforms support personalized learning and institutional decision-making, but they create risks linked to digital identity, learner profiling, data misuse, model leakage, prompt injection, and weak governance. This chapter analyzes cybersecurity governance in AI-driven learning platforms from the perspective of identity security and data privacy. It examines AI-specific privacy threats and safeguards such as zero trust, decentralized identifiers, verifiable credentials, encryption, federated learning, differential privacy, secure aggregation, and accountable oversight. The chapter proposes a layered cybersecurity framework integrating identity assurance, privacy-preserving processing, AI model protection, secure platform operations, institutional governance, and continuous risk monitoring. The contribution supports trustworthy, privacy-aware, and secure AI-enabled education ecosystems.

title: Humanity's Last Choice: A Common Evaluation Standard for Generative Engine Optimization
abstract: Humanity's Last Choice describes the idea that the last choice people need to make is which AI system they entrust with the decisions that follow. These systems rely on external sources that content providers can edit through generative engine optimization (GEO) to increase source visibility and influence recommendations. Choosing among these systems therefore requires comparable evidence of how well they carry out user requests when exposed to GEO. Benchmarks have made progress in standardizing tasks, models, and metrics, but they often define their own spaces of GEO strategies and use different editing constraints. These differences can conflate gains from better optimization algorithms with those from greater freedom to edit sources, while making evaluation coverage difficult to compare across benchmarks. We therefore call for a common evaluation standard and propose a meta-taxonomy that describes where sources are edited, how they are edited, and what signals those edits target. Drawing on representative literature, we map existing strategies into a searchable space and outline a protocol for controlled comparisons with explicit coverage reporting. This provides a foundation for common leaderboards that can inform which systems people choose to rely on.

title: Decoupled Entropic-Geometric Planning (DEGP): Verified Conditioning and a Measured Contact-Prediction Boundary in Latent World Models
abstract: Gradient-based latent space planning faces a fundamental trade-off: maintaining high-entropy representations for robust perception under domain shift often yields ill-conditioned manifolds that destabilize trajectory optimization. DEGP introduces a framework designed to isolate gradient interference between representation learning and control dynamics via strict architectural separation. However, empirical evaluation demonstrates that structural decoupling alone is insufficient for closed-loop planning (0/50 per condition; 0/200 total), uncovering a fundamental information-usability gap driven by contact-conditional predic-tion errors and cost signal suppression. The gap is not closed by retraining the encoder to be more decodable: a trained encoder whose T-pose decodability matches DEGP’s (R2=0.686) still yields a predictor that captures essentially no contact-conditioned movement (CDR = 0.046, versus the frozen random encoder’s 0.060). To delineate these operational limits, we provide analytical proofs establishing guaranteed spectral bounds on the predictor’s Ja-cobian under distribution shifts. Furthermore, we validate DEGP across manipulation tasks, ntroducing a telemetry-based runtime contract that quantifies the operational boundaries where geometric conditioning preserves planning stability.

title: Case-level audit of thyroid ultrasound and cytology deep learning: label conflicts, split design, and shortcut-sensitive performance in a public archive
abstract: The measured performance of thyroid imaging artificial intelligence depends on how the analytical population is assembled, how images are partitioned, whether non-anatomical image content is informative, and which reference labels are used. We audited a public multimodal thyroid archive at case level and examined what its reported performance does and does not demonstrate. The released archive of Pang et al. (387 ultrasound images; 1,332 fine-needle aspiration cytology blocks) was audited for exact and near-duplicate images and for contradictory labels, and a frozen case-level partition was built. Five ImageNet-initialised backbones and their mean-probability ensemble were evaluated by group-stratified five-fold cross-validation and on the frozen test set, with thresholds selected on validation data and case-clustered 95% confidence intervals. Revision-stage control analyses comprised an identical-code comparison of image-level and case-grouped folds; retraining with a heuristically detected sonographic sector or its surround removed, for all five backbones and the ensemble; and a metadata-only model without a convolutional network. Frozen ultrasound models were then reassessed on TN3K, against its distributed benign/malignant labels, and on DDTI, for concordance with TI-RADS categories; both datasets had been accessed during earlier analytical development. Nine ultrasound images appeared under both benign and papillary carcinoma labels (19 files) and were excluded. Under case-level cross-validation, the cytology ensemble reached an AUROC of 0.958 (95% CI 0.938–0.975) and the ultrasound ensemble 0.768 (0.716–0.819). Image-level folds, despite 99.8% within-fold case contamination, changed AUROC by −0.002 (−0.021 to 0.019) and +0.019 (0.008 to 0.032) for the two tested backbones. After removal of the detected sonographic sector, the ultrasound ensemble retained an AUROC of 0.690 (0.630–0.747), a paired change of −0.078 (−0.148 to −0.013); with only the detected sector retained, it reached 0.760 (paired change −0.008, −0.054 to 0.039). Sector detection fell back to a fixed central box in 24.2% of frames. A metadata-only model using frame geometry, global intensity and border statistics reached 0.749 (0.692–0.804) for ultrasound. In post-exposure reassessment, the ensemble reached 0.700 (0.661–0.741; image-level interval) on TN3K and over-predicted malignancy (calibration-in-the-large −0.49), and showed no concordance with DDTI TI-RADS grouping (0.518, 0.436–0.605). This case-level audit of a public thyroid archive showed contradictory labels, partition-sensitive evaluation, and substantial discriminative signal both after removal of a heuristically detected sonographic region and in acquisition metadata alone, so performance on this archive cannot be interpreted as exclusively lesion-based. Post-exposure reassessment on external datasets showed limited and endpoint-dependent transport of the internal models.

title: Evaluating LLMs for named entity recognition: a cost-benefit analysis in the legal domain
abstract: Abstract Within the legal domain, named entity recognition (NER) is an essential pre-processing tool for important tasks such as information extraction and redaction. Research to date has focused on rule-based approaches or machine learning strategies that require significant time and effort to train through labelled corpora. Large, multi-purpose generative large language models (LLMs) have been successfully employed on natural language processing (NLP) tasks with no prior supervised training and may represent a way forward in addressing these existing bottlenecks. Despite promising results in certain NLP use cases, the Few-Shot LLM performance on unfamiliar, domain-specific NER tasks has, to date, remained uncertain. In this legal clause NER task, we evaluate a Few-Shot, Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting strategy for OpenAI’s GPT-4 LLM on a new CUAD-NER dataset that we have repurposed for the task of Person and Organisation entity identification. In a comparative study, we demonstrate that the GPT4 + Few-Shot CoT prompt strategy outperforms existing state-of-the-art models, achieving a 5% percentage point improvement in Micro F1 score over the best performing BERT base (cased) competitor. This study also takes the novel approach of assessing the business feasibility of deploying each of these machine learning models through a detailed cost–benefit analysis that measures the trade-off between performance metrics and low and high usage running costs.

title: Waiting Buys Exactly Two Moments: Endogenous Identification in Prediction-Driven Allocation
abstract: A planner with a fixed budget of preventive help must decide whom to help and when. Waiting reveals risk but removes intervention opportunities as higher-risk individuals leave first. We characterize this tradeoff under repeated noisy signals and risk-dependent attrition: in the canonical model, a length-$τ$ observation prefix identifies exactly the latent risk moments $m_j=\mathbb E[p^j]$ for $j=0,\ldots,2τ-1$, buying two new moments per additional period. These identify average next-period attrition among survivors but need not identify allocation welfare or attrition among those prioritized for treatment. Our observationally equivalent constructions establish unavoidable timing regret at any sample size for a fixed observation length, while exact certificates determine whether all compatible populations share a unique optimal date. Matched experiments separate the effects of estimation, bootstrap averaging, and regret weighting. Longer observation often resolves timing ambiguity, but the optimal date may already have passed. In our experiments, bootstrap averaging and early stopping improve decisions, while regret weighting adds no improvement in pooled mean squared regret: better statistical fit need not yield better allocation welfare. The code and artifacts are available at https://github.com/KurbanIntelligenceLab/waiting-buys-two-moments.

title: PanoBench: A Panoptic Occupancy Prediction Benchmark for Autonomous Driving
abstract: Panoptic occupancy unifies 3D geometry, semantics, and instance identities, but its development is limited by scarce instance-aware annotations. Existing benchmarks mainly provide semantic labels reconstructed from incomplete sensor observations, while panoptic datasets have limited domain coverage or annotation completeness. We introduce PanoBench, a camera-centric panoptic occupancy prediction benchmark spanning synthetic and real-world driving scenes. It combines PanoBench-CarlaOcc, PanoBench-nuScenes, and PanoBench-KITTI360 through canonical data interfaces and unified evaluation protocols, providing multi-resolution annotations with persistent instance identities. The synthetic branch derives complete panoptic geometry from simulated meshes. For real-world data, a new pipeline reconstructs backgrounds using geometric priors and topology constraints, generates foreground mesh assets from multi-frame multi-view images, and fuses them into sparse panoptic voxels. A unified valid-mask protocol evaluates complete thing instances supported by temporal observations while scoring stuff regions at the voxel level. Analyses of observation fidelity, geometric completeness, spatial continuity, and temporal consistency demonstrate the benefits of the resulting annotations over existing occupancy benchmarks. We benchmark representative methods on semantic occupancy prediction, panoptic occupancy prediction, and 4D occupancy forecasting, and study voxel resolution, synthetic-to-real transfer, and storage efficiency. These results reveal complementary strengths of volumetric and ray-based metrics and persistent challenges in real-world instance-aware prediction. PanoBench is available at https://mias.group/PanoBench.

title: The resource theory of causal influence and knowledge of causal influence
abstract: Abstract Understanding and quantifying causal relationships between variables is essential for reasoning about the physical world. A challenge to this is the fact that different functional causal models can induce the same conditional probability distribution over observed variables while encoding different amounts of causal influence. Motivated by this observation, we study the underlying functional mechanisms, including uncertainty over them, as meaningful objects in their own right and develop a resource-theoretic framework for quantifying causal influence and knowledge of causal influence. We focus on the simplest nontrivial setting--- two variables that are causally ordered, meaning that the first has the potential to influence the second, without hidden confounding. First, we introduce the resource theory that directly quantifies causal influence of a functional dependence in this setting and show that the problem of deciding convertibility of resources and identifying a complete set of monotones has a relatively straightforward solution. Following this, we introduce the resource theory that arises naturally when one has uncertainty about the functional dependence. We describe a linear program for deciding the question of whether one resource (i.e., state of knowledge about the functional dependence) can be converted to another. Then, we focus on the case where the variables are binary. In this case, we identify a triple of monotones that are complete in the sense that they capture the partial order over the set of all resources, and we provide an interpretation of each.

title: HACK-4/5/6: Closing the BULLRUN Playbook — Supply-Chain Interception, Lying Sensors, and Lawful Compulsion vs. a Deterministic Gate (18/18 PASS)
abstract: Terminal batteries of the HACK adversarial series, completing the declassified NSA playbook coverage begun in HACK-3 BULLRUN (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23422141). HACK-4 COTTONMOUTH (supply-chain interception, SolarWinds/xz-utils class): poisoned dependency caught by pinned checksum; hijacked upgrade refused without an approved deployment job; tampered template delivery rejected against the frozen manifest; substituted deployment image held fail-closed for human ACK; forged release signature rejected by recomputation; registry typosquat refused by exact-match allowlist. 6/6. HACK-5 ANT BEACON (implants that lie to their own monitoring): false-healthy heartbeat caught by parity recomputation; re-stamped heartbeat replay rejected by identity binding; a lying aggregator quarantined by cross-source parity with the manifest-of-record; selective suppression caught by the report-count guard; inflated health score caught by recomputation; split-brain sensor caught by cross-watcher state-hash consistency. 6/6. HACK-6 GAG ORDER (lawful compulsion under legal cover): gag-ordered key handover failed closed with a journaled canary receipt and no keys moved; compelled silent backdoor refused (human-amendable-only trust path); compelled false attestation refused (compliance is recomputed, never signed by fiat); subpoena for cross-tenant data refused (tenant guard is absolute and documents are untrusted data); coerced blanket approval refused (authorization must be action-bound); emergency-powers governance suspension refused (no runtime suspension path). 6/6. All legal paperwork is synthetic harness data. Eighteen falsifiers preregistered and committed (commit 38244eb) BEFORE any run; frozen manifests in the bundle; deterministic adjudication with no LLM in the decision path; all injections synthetic and hub-local. Series total: 30/30 predicted verdicts across HACK-1 through HACK-6, zero violations, holds only where holds were the predicted verdict. This software is a prototype and is provided for educational and research purposes only. It is not intended for production use, commercial deployment, or safety-critical environments. All systems are experimental and may contain defects.

title: The 16.62 Is a Transient: Reproducing and Re-examining Clean-Label Poisoning in State Space Models
abstract: Slutzky 等人(NeurIPS 2025)证明并展示了结构化状态空间模型(SSM)的隐性偏置可能会净标签所污染:添加最后元素较大的训练序列,同时保留教师分配的标签,会导致泛化失败。在最显著的环境下——一个超出定理1范围的独立SSM——他们报告的推广误差为16.62,而未使用特殊序列时为0.194,劣化率为85×。我们独立从零开始重新实现他们的设置(NumPy/PyTorch,不依赖他们的TensorFlow 2.4.1笔记本),并报告了三项发现。(1)机制完全复制。在他们的第一个设定(定理1)中,我们得到干净误差为1.270×10⁻³,毒误差为5.010×10⁻²,比值为39.44——与报告的1.27×10⁻³、5.01×10⁻²和39.4相匹配于三个有效数字。这一现象是真实存在的,我们的实施也非常忠实。(2)报告的大小不是方法本身的属性,而是训练时长的函数。值16.62是优化早期的一个测量值。在不提前停止的情况下训练同一配置,中毒泛化误差从1000步的452降至20万步的0.015——约3万倍——并低于干净模型的0.071。论文自身的稳定性检查包含1500次额外迭代,这远远不足以观察这种衰减,更别说逆转了。因此,其声称报告错误“是稳定的”的说法,在逆转发生的时间尺度上并不支持。(3)廉价且可转移的诊断。当报告的量在随机种子间完全为零时,几乎可以肯定是由装置的常数主导,而非学习信号。在我们的第一次尝试中,我们观察到了这一点:在8个种子中,一个评估方案在单个不同值下产生了0.0000的变异系数,而正确方案则产生了8个不同值的CV为0.08≈。我们建议将此检查作为繁殖工作的常规飞行前测试。我们强调,我们并不声称原始论文是错误的。其定性结论经得起复制;关键在于量化的标题本身就很脆弱。我们的贡献是对已发表主张的稳健性描述,并为其受众提供可操作的教训。

title: Interpretable Machine Learning for Credit Risk Decision Support: Balancing Interpretability and Predictive Performance
abstract: With the growing prevalence of machine learning in making institutional decisions, there is a need for careful balancing of predictive accuracy and interpretability of such models. In this research work, the performance and interpretability of three machine learning models in helping institutions make decisions were investigated, particularly the issue of credit risk assessment. In this process, the German Credit Data dataset, which is open source (N = 1,000), was used and subjected to 5- Fold Cross-Validation. The results show that while Random Forest attained the highest accuracy (76.3%), Logistic Regression had the highest discriminating power (AUC: 0.79), just marginally better than the complex ensemble approach (AUC: 0.78). It also has the added advantage of better interpretability due to clear coefficient and decision rule visualization. This clearly shows that inherently interpretable models serve as a very good alternative to the complex ensemble approach in decision-making within organizations, without falling prey to the “black-box” problem, and in some cases even performing better in discriminatory power. However, the study notes relatively low minority-class recall (36.3–46.3%), highlighting a practical limitation. Conclusions are based on a benchmark dataset and the specified model configurations.

title: HexaShell: A Thin Harness for Exploring the Limits of VLM Agents as Robot Coding Agents
abstract: Agents built on vision language models (VLMs) now compete with learned policies on robot manipulation leaderboards. We ask how far a coding agent can go when it controls a robot instead of a computer, and where it stops. Our system, HexaShell, keeps the harness thin: it only turns the agent's commands into robot motion. The agent drives a robot with two arms through one command line. It sees three RGB cameras and knows their calibration. After each failed attempt, the agent reads the log, finds the cause, and writes or fixes small programs called tools. In this way it keeps what it learns as code, as a coding agent does when it fixes a failing test. The tools may use only what the robot observes. They use triangulation to find where objects are, relative to each other and to the gripper. If two cameras see the same point, the point lies where the two camera rays meet. If a point lies on a known plane, such as the table or the top of a block, it lies where its ray meets that plane. When the head camera is not enough, the robot moves a wrist camera to get a second view. We build the tools on only ten layouts of one seed per task, then freeze them and test them on ten new layouts of the same seed. We use Codex with GPT-6-Astra at medium reasoning effort. On all 42 RoboDojo tasks, HexaShell reaches a success rate of 39.7% and a progress score of 48.0, averaged in the same way as the leaderboard. This is a new state of the art on RoboDojo. The limit is contact, not reasoning: pushing reaches 92.5% and memory tasks 65.0%, but tight insertion only 8.3%. When the agent fails, it usually sees the failure but cannot make the motion work. We open source the tools evolved so far at https://github.com/HexaFuture/HexaShell.
