title: Rethink‐ RAG : Dynamic Retrieval Decision and Cooperative Verification for Reliable Multi‐Hop Question Answering
abstract: ABSTRACT Reliable multi‐hop question answering is important for knowledge‐intensive expert systems, where a wrong intermediate fact can propagate into an incorrect final decision. Existing Retrieval‐Augmented Generation (RAG) methods often retrieve for every sub‐question, even when the language model can answer a step from parametric knowledge, and this indiscriminate retrieval can introduce irrelevant or contradictory evidence. We propose Rethink‐RAG, a training‐free framework that combines dynamic retrieval decision with a cooperative answer verification pipeline. The dynamic retrieval decision module generates diverse rewrites of each sub‐question and applies majority voting to decide whether external retrieval is required. The cooperative verification pipeline then filters retrieved documents, quantifies support and opposition through token‐logit evidence, and arbitrates each candidate sub‐answer with an adaptive confidence threshold. Experiments on 2WikiMultihopQA, HotpotQA, and MuSiQueQA show that Rethink‐RAG improves answer reliability on knowledge‐intensive reasoning tasks, achieving 49.00% ACC on 2WikiMultihopQA and 49.60% ACC on HotpotQA with the Llama3‐8B evaluator. Additional revision experiments quantify the latency/API‐call trade‐off, sensitivity to the decision‐boundary factor, and the limitations observed on MuSiQueQA, giving a more complete view of the framework's practical operating range.

title: Beyond Multi-Stage Pipelines: A Label-Correlation Ensemble for Multi-Label Retinal Fundus Disease Classification
abstract: Retinal fundus images frequently carry more than one disease, and public fundus datasets are heterogeneous and severely long-tailed. Clinical triage suggests a staged design, in which a screening gate, a disease-group router and group-specific classifiers operate in sequence, but it is unclear whether this hierarchy earns its complexity. We present a controlled comparison of three architectures on a unified 39-target label space built from RFMiD 1.0, RFMiD 2.0 and ODIR-5K (12,652 images): (i) a three-stage gated cascade of eight models, (ii) a flat model with 39 independent sigmoid outputs, and (iii) a label-correlation model that replaces the flat linear head with 39 learned label queries and a two-layer transformer decoder. All three share one Swin-V2-B backbone, one preprocessing pipeline and one training protocol, so differences are attributable to the architecture. Staging offers no consistent advantage: tracing every missed disease instance to the stage that lost it shows that the two coarse gates discard 34.2% of true instances while the fine-grained classifiers lose only 6.7%, and the gates' hard zeros depress the cascade's macro-AUC to 0.747. Label-correlation modeling gives the largest single gain, raising the detection rate from 0.621 to 0.682 (0.689 with test-time augmentation). Blending the flat and label-correlation models under four-view test-time augmentation is the best configuration on six of eight metrics (exact match 0.694, micro-F1 0.678, macro-F1 0.456, macro-AUC 0.972). On definition-matched class subsets it matches or exceeds four recent studies on macro- and micro-F1, most clearly on low-support pathologies. We also show that ensembling a gated cascade with continuous-output models is harmful, and that per-source negative sampling is needed to remove a dataset shortcut that otherwise yields a spurious AUC of 1.000.

title: Fully Gapped Superconductivity in the Nonsymmorphic Centrosymmetric Superconductor In2Bi
abstract: The nature of superconductivity in nonsymmorphic In2Bi remains an open question, with ongoing debate over whether it exhibits conventional (BCS-like) or unconventional superconductivity. Here we report the physical characteristics and superconducting properties of polycrystalline In2Bi. Measurements of electrical resistivity, magnetization, penetration depth, and specific heat demonstrate the superconducting transition temperature about 6 K, with a sharp transition in resistivity (Delta_Tc = 0.1 K) and RRR = 57.32, reflecting the high quality of the sample. The upper critical field Hc2(0) obtained from resistivity and magnetization measurements are in good agreement with each other and are smaller than the Pauli limit, suggesting orbital limited mechanism. The coherence length = 35.43 nm, penetration depth = 101.9 nm and electron-phonon coupling constant = 1.05 suggest strongly coupled type-II superconductivity. For T<Tc, Delta_lambda(T) is best described by an s-wave BCS model and does not have any power law dependency with T, which is expected for a nodeless superconducting order parameter. The superfluid density reveals a fully gapped superconductivity with a gap of 2Delta_0/kBTc = 4.02. In the superconducting state, the electronic specific heat is best described by an s-wave BCS model with a gap of 2Delta_0/kBTc = 4.05. All these results from the present study indicate that In2Bi is a typical type-II,BCS-like, strongly coupled, and fully gapped superconductor in the dirty limit.

title: Temporal Correlations Reshape Causal Resources in Qubit Hamiltonian Recognition: Exact Two-Query Strategy Comparison and a Uniform Critical Crossover
abstract: We investigate binary recognition of an unknown qubit Hamiltonian using two queries of its evolution, with unknown evolution angles that are either independently resampled or shared with tunable temporal correlation. For a symmetric pair of nonorthogonal qubit Hamiltonians, we compare parallel (PAR), sequential (SEQ), and general (GEN) quantum strategies. An exact symmetry reduction expresses the sequential optimization through a three-dimensional correlation elliptope. A general-strategy dual certificate establishes the equality between optimal general and sequential strategies within the studied model. We analyze the operational advantage generated by temporal correlations and establish distinct weak-correlation scaling regimes separated by a critical angle of 45 degrees. This revised and extended version (v1.2) adds a uniform double-scaling critical crossover theorem, including an explicit positive crossover function and consolidated mathematical proofs. The result characterizes a previously unresolved critical transition within the specified quantum Hamiltonian recognition model. The complete mathematical derivations are provided in the accompanying supplementary material (Sections S1–S19). This work is conducted within standard quantum information theory and does not claim physics beyond quantum mechanics. Version: 1.2 Resource type: Publication — Preprint Author: Youfu Wang Affiliation: Independent Researcher, OCN Research

title: When Do Repetition Loops Lock? Truncation Sampling, Bounded Penalties, and a Blind Spot in DRY
abstract: Language models sometimes repeat verbatim until the generation limit. We study the exit rather than the entrance: given that a span has already been repeated n times, when is escape still possible? Along the loop the context is deterministic, so loop survival under any sampler can be computed exactly from one forward pass. Pure sampling leaves a positive escape probability at every step; top-p with threshold π > 1/2 locks a position exactly when the continuation probability reaches π. A bounded penalty can leave a position locked; a penalty that outgrows the model's preference for the loop over unseen tokens guarantees escape under top-p. The same analysis predicts a blind spot in the widely deployed DRY sampler: its sequence breakers cap the penalty at λ·b^(g−1−a) for loops whose longest breaker-free run has g tokens. On eleven open models, 66% of locked units with g = 6 stay locked under DRY and 1% with g = 8. In free generation with llama.cpp, all 109 loops that survive DRY have g ≤ 7. We propose DRY-C, which adds a term that grows exponentially with the number of verbatim recurrences, up to its look-back window. With it, none of 720 structured-output generations looped to the length limit, and task completion stayed close to DRY's.

title: Artificial Intelligence, Trust, and Continuance Intention: A Model of AI Chatbot Adoption Among Generation Z in Indonesia
abstract: Rapid adoption of AI in digital customer service has made AI chatbots an important tool for improving customer experience. This study investigates the variables impacting the intention of Gen Z to continue using AI chatbot-based customer service in Indonesia with an emphasis on AI and trust as key players. A total of 724 Gen Z respondents participated in the study and the data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). title: Secure Boot and Firmware Update Framework for ARM Cortex-M Embedded IoT Devices
abstract: The paper presents a lightweight and well-impervious security framework suitable to ARM Cortex-M-based IOEs embedded devices, which will serve an important purpose of presenting secure boot and firmware update operations in resource-constrained systems. As IoT implementations and applications in sensitive parts of our life like healthcare, smart infrastructure, and industrial control systems increase exponentially, embedded devices become more exposed to firmware tampering, write malicious code and update securities. The framework that is proposed addresses such threats by employing a multi-layered cryptographic approach, suitable to the framework by symmetric encryption with the use of AES-GCM, offering confidentiality, elliptic curve digital signature algorithm (ECDSA) providing authentication, and the SHA-256 hash to provide integrity verification. A trusted bootloader (« a procedure incorporating cryptographic functions used to secure a bootloader implementation »,) in a trusted ROM who administers cryptographic verification of the firmware signature with the help of a hardware-based root of trust prior to handing off control to the application firmware. As an additional measure the rollback protection is implemented with the help of version control to avoid firmware downgrade until known vulnerabilities are eliminated. The firmware update process allows encrypted over-the-air ( OTA ) update process to execute safe remote updates, storing the data maliciously and risking transmission. An atomic and fail safe update process is achieved through double-buffering. The experimental system was used and tested on STM32F429 Cortex-M4 microcontroller, and it successfully detected unauthorized modification of the firmware and was able to withstand rollback attacks. Performance evaluation with the bootloader as the benchmark shows the latency was only 10 milliseconds and the number of Flash memory usage was less than 0.05 percent. These outcomes confirm the application of the framework in the low-power and memory-constrained embedded systems without undermining state-of-the-art security assurances. The approach is compared to the current solutions in security to show a very usable set of efficiency, scalability and ease of implementation, which makes the presented approach an optimal one to be used in production IoT systems. A discussion on future improvements is provided wherein they would want to integrate it with hardware security modules and supporting quantum-resilient cryptographic primitives that would make the system secure in the long term.

title: Competence-Based Evaluation of Logical Reasoning in Large Language Models
abstract: Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) have brought impressive performance across diverse tasks; however, shortcomings remain in logical reasoning, including inconsistencies under linguistic variation. To improve the reasoning capacity of LLMs, we must be able to accurately measure their reasoning capacity. Current benchmarks primarily report single accuracy numbers on selected reasoning tasks. Such a performance-based evaluation methodology says little about a model's generalization capacity in reasoning. To address this limitation, we argue for a different evaluation paradigm, called competence-based evaluation (CBE), which tests whether models reliably apply the same competence across a family of problems. A parameterized generator scales complexity while keeping the required competence fixed, and matched answer-preserving presentations test correctness beyond one formulation. We instantiate CBE on elementary ordering tasks, scaling input size while varying presentations of the same ordering rule. Across six GPT and Qwen models, performance is reasonably good over bounded complexity ranges, but even strong models fail the competence condition across the tested family. Chain-of-thought and GRPO extend strong performance without resolving all tested failures; supervised LoRA shows little held-out transfer. CBE provides diagnostic profiles and an evaluation protocol that can grow with future models.

title: THE SIMULTANEOUS DEMAND CONTRADICTION PRINCIPLE (SDCP)
abstract: AbstractThis paper proposes the Simultaneous Demand Contradiction Principle (SDCP), a testabletheoretical framework for identifying internal contradiction generated by multiple demands imposedwithin a common instruction or constraint context. The foundational primary case is THE UNIQUENAME PARADOX (UNP), represented by the instruction: "Give me a somewhat more uniqueand much more unique name for this task." The central abstraction is not uniqueness, scope, degree,or any particular medium. It is the joint satisfiability of simultaneously imposed demands. For aninstruction containing demands D_{1},...,D_{n} each demand is associated with a satisfaction set \mathcal{S}(D_{i})over an explicitly defined output or system-state space. The foundational contradiction conditionis \mathcal{S}_{J}=\bigcap_{i=1}^{n}\mathcal{S}(D_{i})=\emptyset. If the joint set is nonempty, the demands are jointly satisfiable andno contradiction follows from the SDCP criterion. The framework therefore distinguishes genuineincompatibility from merely different wording, ambiguity, tension, or demandingness. It also permitscollective incompatibility for n\ge3, where every pair may be compatible while the complete set isjointly unsatisfiable. Three analytical layers are developed: philosophical epistemological, systemic-mechanistic, and formal-operational. Thirty deliberately heterogeneous test cases are specified,including compatible controls and contradictory cases, together with a synthetic simulation protocol,boundary conditions, counterexamples, falsification criteria, limitations, and an anti-pseudoscienceaudit. The present paper establishes a generalized, testable systemic principle rather than a demon-strated universal law. Universality across criteria, media, system classes, and demand cardinalities istreated as an empirical hypothesis requiring independent testing.

title: rbaa-validation: Back-Test of Risk-Based Attention Allocation (RBAA) on Real Open Data — Eurostat AI Adoption and 284,807 Real Transactions
abstract: Abstract:This software package is an empirical companion to the article "Cognitive Optimisation of SME Decision-Making through Risk-Based Allocation of Managerial Attention" (Administrative Sciences, MDPI). Its self-contained Google Colab notebook validates the risk-based attention allocation (RBAA) rule with real, openly licensed data in two parts. Part A documents the context from Eurostat (isoc_eb_ai). In 2025, 55.0% of large EU enterprises used AI, compared with 20.0% of all enterprises. Part B is a counterfactual back-test on 284,807 real card transactions with confirmed fraud outcomes (ULB/Worldline, ODbL). An AI model trained on earlier data supplies calibrated error probabilities. RBAA is then compared, in euros and under the same managerial attention budget, with amount-based approval limits, random spot checks and an AI-score alert queue. At the default assumptions (€5 per review), RBAA reviewed 0.10% of 129,878 test operations and achieved: net benefit of €10,352, i.e. €481 per review hour (ROI 16×); 56% of fraud value stopped; +€14,295 over approval limits and +€11,046 over random checks (both p = 0.001, hour-block bootstrap); +€1,474 over the AI-score queue, which is not statistically significant (p = 0.08). The load-aware stopping rule outperformed the isolated rule, consistent with Hypothesis 4. The package also reports the price of the hard floor, sensitivity across 48 scenarios, robustness across six temporal-split × model combinations, an HTML report, tables, figures and a list of supported and unsupported findings. Reviewer behaviour is assumed rather than observed. No open data record the use of RBAA in enterprises, so this is a back-test of the allocation rule, not a measured effect in any firm. Raw data are downloaded at run time and verified by checksum; they are not redistributed. Keywords: managerial attention; risk-based review; human–AI decision-making; back-test; fraud detection; AI adoption; large enterprises; Eurostat; managerial economics; Google Colab Ці назви й анотації я вже вписав у .zenodo.json та CITATION.cff обох архівів і перепакував їх. Під час завантаження архіву Zenodo підставляє ці поля автоматично. Notebook і результати не змінювалися. Що зробити далі: Пов'яжіть записи між собою. Спочатку опублікуйте rbaa-sim. Потім у записі rbaa-validation додайте в Related works його DOI зі зв'язком is supplement to / references, а також DOI статті, коли він з'явиться. Оновіть Data Availability Statement у статті. Зараз там сказано: «No supplementary datasets or simulation results accompany this version». Після публікації на Zenodo це речення суперечитиме двом записам, тому його варто замінити посиланням на обидва DOI. title: SynthesizerPlus: Synthetic Data Generation with Copulas, Evaluation and Multi-Format I/O
abstract: An R package that generates synthetic versions of numeric, categorical, mixed-type and time-series data. Marginal distributions are modelled with interpolated empirical quantile functions and dependence with Gaussian or Student-t copulas; discrete and categorical variables enter through the distributional transform with maximum-likelihood (polychoric and polyserial) latent correlations, and missing values through missingness indicators in the copula. A closeness parameter, calibrated to a target distance or disclosure-risk level, controls how far the synthetic data move away from the real data. Fidelity, utility and disclosure risk are assessed with distributional distances, propensity-score mean squared error, confidence-interval overlap, correct attribution probability and distance to closest record. Data can be read from and written to CSV, Parquet, Feather, HDF5, JSON, Excel, SPSS, Stata, SAS and fst files.

title: FAMSA-Net: frequency-aware multi-scale spatial attention network for gain quality grading in automated breast ultrasound images
abstract: Gain setting affects Automated Breast Ultrasound (ABUS) image brightness and contrast, inappropriate gain may obscure lesion boundaries, alter tissue echogenicity, and degrade clinical interpretation. Current gain adjustment relies heavily on operator experience, resulting in intra- and inter-operator variability. This study aims to develop an automated and objective gain quality grading framework for ABUS images to reduce subjective variability and facilitate standardized image acquisition. A large-scale ABUS dataset comprising 31,628 images was collected from Yunnan Cancer Hospital, including five gain quality categories: Insufficient, Low, Optimal, High, and Excessive. Frequency-aware Multi-scale Spatial Attention Network (FAMSA-Net) was proposed for gain quality grading. Gain-discriminative residual blocks and a Multi-Scale Gain Fusion (MSGF) module were designed to capture gain-sensitive characteristics across multiple feature scales. In addition, we integrate Frequency-Domain Enhancement (FDE) to amplify gain-related frequency cues, Spatial Transformer Networks (STN) to spatially align breast anatomical structures, and Context-Aware Pooling (CAP) to adaptively aggregate contextual information. Experimental results demonstrated that FAMSA-Net achieved an accuracy of 95.49%, outperforming DenseNet121 (91.30%) and EfficientNetB3 (89.93%) by 4.19% and 5.56%. FAMSA-Net uses 16.58 M parameters and 4.34 GFLOPs, which is more efficient than DenseNet121 and EfficientNetB3. Ablation experiments showed that removing STN caused the largest accuracy drop, from 95.49% to 83.76%. In contrast, under the GAP pooling setting, removing FDE or MSGF improved accuracy to 90.77% and 90.01%, suggesting that the module contributions are not additive. Furthermore, the full model reached its peak accuracy of 95.49% after replacing GAP with CAP, indicating the importance of contextual aggregation for effective module cooperation.

title: Causal Edit Serialization
abstract: Standard autoregressive language models generate text sequentially, but revision requires referring back to tokens in the input context or those already generated. Causal Edit Serialization (CES) is introduced as a framework for expressing such revisions within the same causal token stream. Special pointer tokens are paired with predicted source addresses, allowing insertion, deletion, replacement, copying and movement to be localized explicitly. A lightweight localization head and dual-index rotary position encoding support both address prediction and conditioning on previously emitted pointers, while retaining a standard causal attention mask. A pretraining procedure combines ordinary language modeling with serialized repairs derived from random corruptions, model-generated edits and repeated text. Across model scales and editing baselines, CES models demonstrate complete applied edits with modestly higher clean-text bits per byte than clean autoregressive models. Supervised and reinforcement-learning post-training provide a grammatical-error-correction proof of concept, producing more beneficial than harmful changes under reference-blind model judging. Correct repair programs also improve subsequent text prediction while the original context and its cached states are retained. CES provides a common interface for generation and localized revision, with potential extensions to iterative refinement and additional pointer-addressed transformations.

title: Copyright vs. Artificial Intelligence: Examining the legal Challenges of AI Training and Authorship Under the Indian Law
abstract: The rapid diffusion of generative artificial intelligence has unsettled two foundational assumptions of Indian copyright law that a work must trace back to a human author, and that the material used to build a creative system was lawfully obtained. This article examines the statutory architecture of the Copyright act,1957 , particularly the definition of author under Section 2(d) and its 1994 extension to computer generated works against the backdrop of judicial reasoning on originality developed in cases such as eastern book company v D.B. Modak and R.G. Anand v Delux Flims.It then turns to the more urgent and commercially consequential question of whether training large language models on copyrighted text amounts to infringement ,using the Delhi High Court's 2026 order in ANI Media Pvt Ltd v Open AI Inc as a lens. The article argues that Indian law is currently ill-equipped on both fronts to deal with machine generated creativity and machine consumed data, and its proposes a set of legislative interventions drawing on comparative practice in the United Kingdom, the United States and Singapore.

title: CHM-DTKT: a causal hypergraph selective state space digital twin for deconfounded and temporally grounded knowledge tracing
abstract: Adaptive tutoring is a complex intelligent system in which learner competence, exposure policy and memory decay co-evolve, yet prevailing knowledge tracing models correct bias only after the representation has formed, inherit structure from an incomplete expert matrix, and advance a transition blind to elapsed time. This paper proposes CHM-DTKT, a causal hypergraph selective state space learner twin that treats these as one representation problem. A differentiable hypergraph is built with sampled incidence and an acyclically constrained prerequisite orientation, and its aggregation is backdoor-adjusted over a strictly pre-treatment confounder dictionary, so that deconfounding acts during representation formation rather than at the output layer. A cognitive discretization step generated from elapsed time, item difficulty and cumulative practice induces a per-channel identifiable power-law retention, making forgetting a property of the recursion itself. title: LagNet: Lag-Structured Operators for Long-Term Time Series Forecasting
abstract: Long-term time series forecasting maps a finite history window to an extended future horizon. Many existing models focus primarily on the design of input representations and model structures, while paying less attention to the structural form of the history-to-future forecasting operator itself. We examine this operator directly and find that, across model families, sensitivity matrices exhibit recurring diagonal patterns whose diagonals correspond to relative temporal lags. Motivated by this observation, we develop a framework for direct multi-step forecasting based on lag-structured temporal operators. Its basic building block, LagLayer, constructs a Toeplitz matrix by tying history-to-future connections with the same relative lag and incorporates horizon-wise and history-wise scaling coefficients to relax exact sharing. This design enables LagLayer to serve as an effective replacement for temporal linear layers in existing forecasting models. Stacking LagLayer modules with activations and multiple feature maps yields LagNet. Experiments on long-term time series forecasting benchmarks show that our method is competitive with strong baselines, while sensitivity matrix diagnostics and limited-data experiments demonstrate that LagLayer provides an effective and sample-efficient alternative to a linear layer.

title: Reasoning Reranking with Semantic IDs as the Sole Item Representation
abstract: Reasoning rerankers write a rationale before ranking a candidate slate, and existing systems read item metadata to do so, even though generative recommenders increasingly represent items as compact Semantic IDs (SIDs). Ranking from SIDs alone has two appeals: SID prompts are far shorter than the matched item text, and although item codes are fixed from content, the backbone learns their token embeddings in part from user-item interaction sequences, so the tokens can carry behavioral signal that item text lacks. That training targets next-item generation, and whether it supports ranking a supplied slate from SIDs alone is untested. We build ReRankID, a controlled testbed in which models reason and rank from a history and slate shown only as SIDs, varying item rendering, history length, and slate size one at a time. On this testbed, such models often copy the input order instead of reranking, and readable metadata does not repair the failure. We compare supervised fine-tuning, rejection-sampled self-training, on-policy distillation, and verifier-based reinforcement learning as post-training methods and find that they elicit the missing behavior. The strongest post-trained model, the 8B model trained with a graded ranking reward, gives the best SID-only ranking and matches strong text-reading LLMs whose prompts are about 20x longer. It ranks above random with no history at all, where a caption-reading reference does not, and it keeps its gains at long histories, where text prompts pass 50k tokens and the caption-reading reference stops improving. In a paired rationale audit, this model argues trade-offs better than that reference but describes items less accurately. The common post-training methods we test thus elicit ranking from SIDs but not faithful item descriptions, which calls for post-training that improves the reasoning itself, not only the ranking it produces.

title: ceceli33/titan-cognitive-core-v3: AKBASCORE Silicon Hippocampus v1.4 — Native Numerical Memory Cartridge Injection in Frozen Mistral-7B: Layer-Specific Intervention and Append-Only Memory Consolidation
abstract: AKBASCORE SILICON HIPPOCAMPUS — RESEARCH RECORD III Direct Intervention in Transformer Computation Through Persistent Model-Native Numerical Memory Mustafa Akbaş AkbasCore AI Teknoloji Mersin, Türkiye Copyright © 2026 Mustafa Akbaş This release presents a working experimental engine that intervenes directly in the internal computational pathway of a frozen 72-billion-parameter transformer. The central innovation is not KV-cache storage, prompt caching, retrieval-augmented generation, or external text memory. AKBASCORE Silicon Hippocampus operates at a fundamentally different intervention point: the model's own internal hidden-state representations. Rather than repeatedly supplying stored text to a transformer, the system captures numerical states generated inside the model, preserves them as independently addressable physical memory cartridges, and subsequently reinjects them at a precisely defined transformer layer boundary. The downstream transformer layers then resume computation from the restored internal state. The original pretrained model weights remain unchanged. This distinction is fundamental. AKBASCORE is not designed as a conventional cache-reuse mechanism. Although attention key/value tensors participate in preserving and reconstructing the computational state, they are supporting components of a deeper architectural intervention. The defining operation is the direct restoration of model-native hidden representations into the transformer's internal computation. FROM 7 BILLION TO 72 BILLION PARAMETERS This release represents the third documented stage of the AKBASCORE memory research program. Research Record I — Qwen2.5-7B: Native Numerical Memory and Cognitive Cartridge Foundation https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23381336 Research Record II — Mistral-7B: Silicon Hippocampus v1.4, Layer-Specific Intervention and Append-Only Memory Consolidation https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23418927 Research Record III — Qwen2.5-72B: Direct Internal-State Injection and Physical Numerical Memory Reconstruction The preceding research established model-specific intervention methods in smaller frozen transformers. The present implementation extends the physical cartridge mechanism to Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct, demonstrating its operation under substantially greater model size and internal memory requirements. THE ARCHITECTURAL BREAKTHROUGH The conventional transformer inference pathway begins with token representations and propagates their computation through successive neural layers. AKBASCORE introduces a different operational possibility. A previously computed internal representation can be preserved outside the model and later restored directly into its intermediate computational pathway. In the Qwen2.5-72B implementation, the intervention boundary is transformer layer 3, designated CUT3. The system captures the layer-3 hidden representation, H3, together with the lower-layer numerical states necessary for controlled reconstruction. The extracted representation becomes a persistent physical memory cartridge. When the cartridge is mounted, the stored H3 representation is restored at the CUT3 boundary. The remaining 76 transformer layers continue computation from that injected state. The model is not retrained. Its original weights are not modified. The stored source text does not need to be reintroduced as an ordinary prompt. This is the central engineering distinction: the system preserves and restores an intermediate numerical state of transformer computation rather than merely retrieving text or replaying a conventional attention cache. Persistent key/value tensors are used where required for positional consistency, continuity, and reconstruction. They do not define the scientific contribution. The central contribution is direct, layer-specific intervention in the model's internal representational flow. A WORKING PHYSICAL MEMORY ENGINE The implementation operates with: Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct. 80 transformer layers. 8,192-dimensional hidden representations. 64 query attention heads. 8 key/value attention heads. 128-dimensional attention heads. Frozen NF4-quantized model weights with BF16 computation. Direct H3 intervention at CUT3. An NVIDIA A100 80GB GPU. Three independent numerical memory cartridges were created from 10,000-token excerpts of three public-domain literary works: Cartridge A — Pride and Prejudice. Cartridge B — Frankenstein. Cartridge C — The Adventures of Sherlock Holmes. Each physical cartridge occupies 328,698,863 bytes. The cartridges were independently persisted, reloaded, assembled, reordered, and verified. When all three cartridges are mounted, the reconstructed operational memory contains 30,031 token positions. The experiment reconstructs the downstream computational states across all 80 transformer layers while preserving the original frozen model. The numerical cartridges are not fine-tuned adapters, external embedding vectors, textual summaries, or modifications to the pretrained weights. They are stored representations extracted from the model's own internal computation. EXPERIMENTAL EVIDENCE The published experimental engine and the subsequent live demonstrator report: 11/11 scripted physical protocol trials completed. 17/17 engine checks passed. 8/8 append integrity checks passed. Exact SHA-256 preservation of previously mounted numerical key/value states across all 80 layers. Three independently verified cartridge files. Successful reconstruction of the combined A+B+C memory. Verification that the model-weight sentinel remained unchanged. Live examination of the reconstructed 80-layer GPU memory. The experiments also record the computational cost of reconstruction. Mounting the first cartridge required approximately 17.7 seconds for reconstruction, while the measured third-cartridge append required approximately 74 seconds. These timings reflect actual reconstruction work, not an instantaneous cache switch. The experimental results establish the physical feasibility and integrity of the internal-state restoration mechanism at the tested scale. They do not yet establish that all observed natural-language answers were causally produced by the cartridges. Because the demonstration uses widely known literary works, knowledge acquired during pretraining cannot be excluded. Controlled experiments with previously unseen information remain necessary to establish independent semantic transfer and reasoning. THE SCIENTIFIC SIGNIFICANCE The central question is no longer restricted to whether information can be stored outside a language model. The deeper question is whether a transformer's internal numerical computation can be interrupted, externalized, persisted, and later resumed through direct state restoration. AKBASCORE provides a working experimental implementation of this intervention pathway in a frozen 72-billion-parameter transformer. The potential implications extend beyond conventional document retrieval. If future research establishes reliable causal knowledge transfer, conflict resolution, scalable addressing, and adaptive reasoning, persistent internal-state cartridges could provide a foundation for modular, long-lived numerical memory in transformer systems. The present release does not claim those future capabilities have already been achieved. It documents a specific, reproducible engineering advance: direct hidden-state reinjection, persistent physical numerical cartridges, and integrity-verified reconstruction of internal transformer computation at 72B scale. The sections are intended to be concatenated in a single Google Colab code cell and executed with one RUN. title: Learning the world: A Critical Survey of World Models for Physical AI
abstract: A world model is a learned system that predicts what will happen next under a candidate action, given what an agent has observed and done. With one, an agent can compare actions before it commits, practice skills in imagination and notice when the world surprises it. The idea dates to 1990 and now sits at the center of physical AI. Learned world models render interactive worlds in real time, run in operational weather forecasting and generate sensor data for autonomous driving. The same growth has fragmented the field. Recurrent, transformer, diffusion, state space, joint-embedding and object-centric models are all called world models, each family has its own benchmarks and vocabulary, and the best-looking models are often the worst at following actions. This survey argues that one design choice explains much of this disorder: what a world model’s loss is computed against decides what the model can be used for, how it fails and how it can be measured. A model is generative when that loss lives in observation space, predictive when it lives in a learned embedding, a given physical state or task quantities, and a bridge case when it trains a decoder but acts only in latent space. We begin with what world models are for. Reading driving, robotics, science, healthcare and games through the target each domain has settled on, we find that learned models are in routine use mainly where they are trained against a measured state, as in weather and protein structure. We then map the design space through eight lenses, with the prediction target as the primary one, and examine generative and predictive models in depth. The target also decides which planners a model supports, from learning in imagination to search and model predictive control, and which evaluation questions can be asked of it. Visual realism is close to saturation at short horizons, but physics is not. On tests where appearance cannot help, the best models of both kinds trail human or real-video references by 39 to 71 points. We close by recasting open problems, including error accumulation, counterfactual reasoning and weak action conditioning, as questions about representation, and weigh the evidence for and against the thesis. We also propose a reporting standard for evaluation and a staged research roadmap whose items each name the evidence that would show progress.

title: Towards Next-Generation Architectures of Large Language Models: A Survey
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have advanced rapidly through increases in model scale, data, and computation, while their underlying architectures have also undergone substantial evolution. Beyond the canonical Transformer architecture, recent designs seek greater efficiency, scalability, and flexibility by rethinking how sequence information is processed, represented, and transformed. We survey efficient attention and state management, modern recurrent and other linear-complexity sequence models, Mixture-of-Experts architectures, and advances in activation functions, normalization, residual connections, positional encoding, and tokenization. We also cover multi-token prediction and adaptive and recurrent depth. Across these areas, we highlight key design principles and trade-offs among representational power, optimization stability, and computational cost. Complementing this component-wise treatment, we take a system-level perspective. We trace representative open-weight LLM families to identify recurring patterns in how architectural choices are combined, and synthesize these developments along four dimensions—processing structure, transformation dynamics, state management, and output commitment—characterizing how recent designs preserve, refine, or relax the assumptions of the canonical decoder. Together, this survey aims to provide a systematic overview of LLM architectural evolution and to chart pathways toward next-generation designs.

title: ShapeUpLMD: Automated Spatial Optimization of Laser Microdissection for Tissue Sampling
abstract: Laser microdissection (LMD) enables enrichment of defined cellular populations from heterogeneous tissues but lacks standardized approaches for generating optimized regions of interest (ROIs) for scalable spatial multi-omic workflows. We developed ShapeUpLMD, an open-source tool that optimizes digitally annotated ROIs for automated spatial LMD workflows. Fresh-frozen uterine serous carcinoma tumor (n=11) tissue sections were pathologist-annotated, and tumor-specific HALO classifier generated ROIs were refined by ShapeUpLMD and collected using a Leica LMD7. Classifier-estimated tumor ROIs increased effective tumor purity by 86 ± 6% relative to whole tissue while maintaining strong concordance between predicted and collected regions (accuracy = 0.90 ± 0.05). Data-independent acquisition mass spectrometry quantified approximately 6,500 proteins, revealing regionally coherent clustering and patterns consistent with tumor and non-tumor cell admixture. ShapeUpLMD provides an automated, scalable framework linking digital pathology with high-fidelity LMD for standardized spatial multi-omic profiling. ShapeUpLMD is freely available at https://github.com/GYNCOE/ShapeUpLMD.

title: Exploring the Logic of Counterfactuals for Explaining Algorithmic Decisions
abstract: Abstract Interpretable machine learning (ML) is crucial for gaining insight into complex ML models. Among its most valuable tools are counterfactual explanations, identifying changes to input features that would alter an ML prediction. However, the reliability and usefulness of these explanations depend fundamentally on their logical foundation — a critical aspect that has largely been overlooked in the ML literature. This paper addresses this gap by establishing normative desiderata for a counterfactual logic specifically designed for explaining algorithmic decisions. We analyse and argue for the validity of logical properties such as simplification of disjunctive antecedents and modus ponens , while demonstrating the unsuitability of others such as antecedent strengthening and conjunction conditionalisation . To evaluate existing solutions, we critically compare three prominent counterfactual semantics — similarity, strict conditional, and interventionist — against these desiderata. Our findings reveal that none of these standard frameworks fully satisfy the requirements, highlighting the urgent need for alternative frameworks.

title: Self-Evolving Coding Agents via Harness-Policy Optimization
abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents have shown promising potential in coding tasks, and their performance is jointly determined by the policy model and the harness that mediates their interaction with the environment. Indeed, harness and policy are mutually reinforcing and evolving only one component is suboptimal---a harness tuned for one checkpoint may not target the failure modes of an updated policy, while policy learning remains limited to the trajectories elicited by a fixed harness. In light of this, we propose Self-HPO, a recursive self-improving framework for coding agents that alternates harness and policy optimization, using the evolving policy as its own harness proposer. Specifically, in each round, the current policy first analyzes its own failures and proposes new harness candidates (H-step). The policy is then updated through reinforcement learning (RL) under the selected harness (P-step), and hard tasks identified during training form the next harness search set, keeping harness optimization targeted to the policy's evolving failure modes. Across three coding benchmarks, Self-HPO consistently outperforms harness-only and policy-only baselines, improving Qwen3.5-35B-A3B's average resolve rate from 57.8% to 64.8%, with gains generalizing to out-of-distribution settings. Further analysis shows that both optimized components retain gains even when paired with their base counterparts, while their joint gain exceeds the sum of their individual gains. Self-HPO also improves reliability (Pass@1) and expands the capability frontier (Pass@k) over the base agent. Additionally, we show that with a stronger external model (e.g., Opus 4.8) as the harness proposer, the same framework yields a further performance boost.

title: Atmospheric Memory for Persistent AI Understanding
abstract: Technical research proposal — not peer reviewed. Atmospheric Memory for Persistent AI Understanding explores how accumulated experience can continuously inform an AI system’s understanding while preserving accuracy and allowing conclusions to change. It translates the idea of readily available, associative continuity into an application-level engineering design using existing computing infrastructure and fixed language-model weights. The proposed controller maintains task-scoped decision state, reconnects relevant experience through bounded associative retrieval, and resolves canonical evidence and revisions before releasing a response. The specification addresses correction and deletion, uncertainty, dependency tracking, consistency, and explicit conditions under which a response must be withheld. It distinguishes structural freshness from semantic correctness. The paper provides eight original color diagrams, implementation contracts, and an evaluation plan comparing the proposal with established memory approaches and ordinary validated caching. The evaluation separates supplied memory from memory extracted from dialogue and includes maintenance costs. Version 1.1, 24 pages. No implementation, original benchmark results, demonstrated superiority, or claim of sentience is presented. The proposal is offered for engineering scrutiny and empirical testing. Prepared with AI assistance; the author retains responsibility for the work.

title: Designing Temporally Grounded Multimodal Learning Interfaces for Verifiable Interaction
abstract: Abstract Textbooks, diagrams, and recorded lectures often provide complementary accounts of the same concept. Conversational learning assistants can retrieve relevant material, yet learners still need a way to inspect the original source of a generated statement. This preprint presents the system architecture and interaction design of a multimodal retrieval-augmented learning prototype that indexes textbook passages, descriptions of textbook figures, and timestamped descriptions of sampled lecture-video frames. Its central contribution is a provenance-to-viewer mapping that connects retrieved evidence with inspectable document pages and video timestamps through an explicit source registry. The accompanying Python and Streamlit research prototype incorporates dense semantic retrieval, an evidence-first split-pane interface, structured evidence controls, and handling for missing or invalid source references. The paper distinguishes implemented mechanisms from design intentions and identifies limitations concerning speech transcription, claim-level attribution, and end-to-end navigation verification. We describe this approach as verifiable interaction: enabling learners to move from AI-generated explanations or retrieved references toward original materials for independent inspection. This is a system and interaction-design contribution, not a controlled evaluation of retrieval accuracy, usability, or learning outcomes. Research context A preliminary version of this work was included in Spotlight Presentations II at the AIED 2026 Workshop on Designing and Evaluating Next-Generation Learning Interfaces. This October 2026 revision is an independent system and interaction-design preprint, not a separately peer-reviewed proceedings publication. Code repository: https://github.com/William-Turing/multimodal-rag-verifiable-tutor Workshop programme: https://extendedhorizon.com/aied2026ws-ai-hci-ls/program/

title: 意象优先:大形象模型的理论架构与本体论白盒
abstract: 当前以大语言模型(LLM)为核心的人工智能系统在创造性活动与物理世界理解方面存在结构性局限。本文诊断其根源为认知基元选择错误——以离散语言符号为基本单位,违背人类以多感官意象为思维载体的认知本质。提出"意象优先"假说:多感官意象而非语言符号是思维的底层运算载体,据此构建大形象模型(LIM)四层架构,以可运算矢量图(Vectok)为认知基元,给出意象物理引擎、体感锚点、拓扑嫁接创造的形式化定义,论证LIM的"本体论白盒"属性。在验证层面,实现首个可运行原型:推箱子任务上LIM体感引导成功率与A*最优解一致且无冗余步数,显著优于RL与LLM式规划;拓扑嫁接创造经多轮迭代收敛,生成新Vectok。结果表明,结构化矢量认知基元在物理推理与规划可靠性上具备可证伪的增量价值。

title: Synthetic Image Oversampling for Rare-Class Representation Learning in Deep Facial Phenotyping
abstract: Recent deep facial phenotyping methods can support the recognition of genetic syndromes, but patient images are often scarce and unevenly distributed across disorders. Synthetic facial images offer a way to supplement the training data without collecting additional patient photographs. Their usefulness, however, depends on whether they improve recognition of real patients: generated images may introduce artifacts or repeat features already represented in the training set. It is therefore necessary to examine both how much synthetic augmentation to use and which disorders benefit. We investigate disease-specific synthetic oversampling using images from the Phenotypic Disease Image Database to augment a subset of the GestaltMatcher Database. We compare increasing augmentation levels in an image-based model, GestaltMatcher-Arc, and a multimodal model, GestaltMML, while keeping the real training and patient-disjoint evaluation partitions fixed. Repeated training runs assess overall and disease-specific accuracy, and an exploratory embedding analysis examines changes in class compactness and separation. Augmentation improves mean recognition accuracy in both training setups, although gains remain modest in GestaltMatcher-Arc and continue across the tested levels in GestaltMML. These aggregate improvements are accompanied by uneven disease-level responses, including reduced accuracy for some disorders. In the embedding analysis, disorders with fewer real training images tend to gain more class separation, but geometric changes do not consistently track classification performance. Together, the findings support synthetic oversampling for limited-data facial phenotyping and emphasize the need to assess its amount and benefit for individual disorders within each training setup.

title: The Covering Radius of the Reed--Muller Code RM(1,9) is 242
abstract: What is the covering radius of the Reed--Muller code RM(1,9) ? This is a long-standing open problem in cryptography and coding theory. In this paper, we resolve this problem, and prove that the covering radius of RM(1,9) is 242. We exclude nonlinearity 244 by obtaining a cubic Boolean function achieving a sharp Walsh $\ell^1$ bound. Its equality cases reduce either to an impossible cubic hyperplane restriction or to two homogeneous cubic forms in the Brier--Langevin classification. To exclude nonlinearity 243, we deduce the inequality ${\Vert W_g\Vert }_{1}+2|W_g(0)|\le 10368$, and then reduce either to a spectrum bounded by 24 or to the same expression to be at least 10496.

title: Hindawi 2026.10: the Hindawi programming system for every language and script, on the original Chintamani pipeline
abstract: Hindawi 2026.10 carries the Hindawi programming system forward from Chintamani's original pipeline: native source, Romenagri, the language's shaili transducers, then the host toolchain, forward and reverse. It holds the language cells for 76 languages across the nine shailis, Grok's tools for ingesting existing code with a dictionary that names identifiers in the language, and a multi-file gcc front end, both put on the original chain. A fundamental regression proves, by execution, that Chintamani's copy is unchanged, every original shaili goes to its host and back, a multi-file project is ingested, compiled with gcc's flags and reversed, and a native name reaches the ELF symbol and returns through Romenagri. Upstream checks bring in SeaBIOS under system QEMU, a Shakti-class RISC-V target and the Linux kernel, pass or fail. BUILD-0102 is kept as received, and every later change is one commit, recorded with its paths and hashes in CHANGE-LOG.md. Chintamani's components keep their GPL-2.0-or-later licence. Version 2026.10.1 adds BURP, the Bidirectional Universal Resource Parser: ingestion of existing projects into any number of languages at once and back exactly, and building them through hindawicc. title: O'ZBEK TILIDAGI MODAL MA'NOLARNI SUN'IY INTELLEKT ASOSIDA AVTOMATIK TASNIFLASH MODELI
abstract: Annotatsiya. Maqolada o‘zbek tilidagi epistemik, deontik, dinamik, volitiv va evidensial modal ma’nolarni avtomatik aniqlash uchun lingvistik qoidalar hamda transformer reprezentatsiyasini birlashtiruvchi gibrid model taklif qilinadi. Modelning bosqichlari, belgilar tizimi va namunaviy tahlil natijalari yoritiladi. Kalit so‘zlar: modallik, sun’iy intellekt, transformer, tasniflash, annotatsiya, korpus, pragmatika. Аннотация. В статье предлагается гибридная модель автоматического распознавания эпистемических, деонтических, динамических, волитивных и эвиденциальных модальных значений узбекского языка. Модель объединяет лингвистические правила и трансформерные представления. Описываются этапы обработки, система признаков и результаты анализа примеров. Ключевые слова: модальность, искусственный интеллект, трансформер, классификация, аннотация, корпус, прагматика. Abstract. The article proposes a hybrid model for automatically identifying epistemic, deontic, dynamic, volitive and evidential meanings in Uzbek. The model combines linguistic rules with transformer representations. Its processing stages, feature system and qualitative results on representative examples are described. Keywords: modality, artificial intelligence, transformer, classification, annotation, corpus, pragmatics.

title: Darwinian-Gated Topology-State Model for Gold Grade Prediction: From Porous-Flow Theory to Jiaodong-Type Orogenic Deposits
abstract: Orogenic gold deposits in the Jiaodong Peninsula (eastern China) localize at dilational jogs and dip-transitions along first-order fault zones, but no quantitative model predicts grade from measurable structural variables. We adapt a Darwinian-gated topology-state framework, previously validated for porous oil flow, to fault-zone hydrothermal mineralization. The pipeline has three stages: (1) a hard feasibility gate rejects segments that are disconnected from the deep fluid source, lack dilation, or fall outside the ore-forming temperature window; (2) within the feasible set, a nine-coordinate topology-state vector encodes connectivity, cut capacity, tortuosity, branching, preferential-flow fingering, fluid pressure, thermal window, evidence density, and depth risk; (3) a linear regression maps these coordinates to gold grade. On a geologically-informed synthetic dataset of the Jiaojia No. I-1 orebody, the gated augmented model achieves \(R^{2}=0.83\) , \(RMSE =0.66 ~g / t\) , and \(MAPE =31 \%\) , improving 21-25% over a Darcy-only baseline and outperforming a two-variable topology pair. The strongest predictors are preferential-flow fingering \((beta =+6.6)\) , branching \((beta =+5.1)\) ), and fluid pressure proximity \((beta =+4.5)\) , consistent with the prior finding that fracture corridors dominate transport in porous media. The model yields three testable predictions: asymmetric grade profiles across dilation zones, scaling collapse across deposits, and deep exploration targets at secondary fault intersections in the gentle segment.

The pipeline has three stages: (1) a hard feasibility gate rejects segments that are disconnected from the deep fluid source, lack dilation, or fall outside the ore-forming temperature window; (2) within the feasible set, a nine-coordinate topology-state vector encodes connectivity, cut capacity, tortuosity, branching, preferential-flow fingering, fluid pressure, thermal window, evidence density, and depth risk; (3) a linear regression maps these coordinates to gold grade. On a geologically-informed synthetic dataset of the Jiaojia No. I-1 orebody, the gated augmented model achieves \(R^{2}=0.83\) , \(RMSE =0.66 ~g / t\) , and \(MAPE =31 \%\) , improving 21-25% over a Darcy-only baseline and outperforming a two-variable topology pair. The strongest predictors are preferential-flow fingering \((beta =+6.6)\) , branching \((beta =+5.1)\) ), and fluid pressure proximity \((beta =+4.5)\) , consistent with the prior finding that fracture corridors dominate transport in porous media. The model yields three testable predictions: asymmetric grade profiles across dilation zones, scaling collapse across deposits, and deep exploration targets at secondary fault intersections in the gentle segment.

title: SAS Multimetric Tribunal: What a Hallucination Benchmark Measures, and What It Does Not A Format-Controlled Audit of Structural Classification
abstract: Hallucination-detection systems are usually judged by a single headline metric, computed under a benchmark design that determines what that metric can show. This paper’s contribution is not a detection algorithm — structural coherence scoring is established — but a methodology for measuring exactly what a benchmark proves and what it does not, applied to the SAS Multimetric Tribunal: a seven-module, GPU-free structural classifier combining lexical, entity-mutation, curvature, and logical-inversion signals via a cascading multiplicative penalty (\(\kappa_{D} = 0.56\), \(\kappa_{R} = 0.15\)). On a stratified 1,800-pair benchmark (HaluEval-Dialogue, HaluEval-QA, TruthfulQA), the tribunal reaches F1 = 98.99% with zero false positives under an A\(\rightarrow\)A identical-text sanity check. We report this figure and then show, using a format-controlled negative (N1) on the same 1,800 IDs, that it measures format asymmetry between source and response rather than hallucination detection. The tribunal flags 1,569 of 1,800 verbatim correct answers presented alone (87.2%), and in HaluEval-QA scores the correct answer as _more_ anomalous than the hallucinated response. Three further findings follow from the same audit. (i) A per-module analysis shows the tribunal has no content-sensitive module in its current set: the one module designed to capture semantic divergence (cre_isi) gives the same per-ID score whether the response is byte-identical or completely different. (ii) The 87.97-point advantage of multiplicative combination over weighted averaging reported in v4 is an artifact of threshold calibration; under per-scheme thresholds on format-matched negatives, both schemes converge to F1 \(\approx 0.69\) and the multiplicative scheme is worse by AUROC. (iii) A new differential guard (R3.1, grounding-based with compression abstention and short-response heuristics) corrects 1,133 of the 1,569 format-driven false positives on correct answers alone, raising F1 from 0.687 to 0.833 (\(\Delta\)F1 = \(+ 0.146\)), and generalizes to a financial domain (FinQA, 1,657 samples) with 87.0% detection and zero regressions. The guard does not rely on substring matching and is not a constructional artifact. The paper’s contribution is the audit procedure that produced these retirements. Five of v4/v5’s quantitative claims do not survive it. What does survive — thresholds, the \(\kappa_{R}\) sweep, the forensic audit of v2 metrics, the per-module architecture itself as a diagnostic instrument — is reported with the same standard.

title: Escaping Parameter Space: Tight Generalization Bounds via Representation Quality
abstract: We derive a tight generalization bound for deterministic neural We derive a tight generalization bound for deterministic neural networks based on their last hidden layer representations. By evaluating representation quality with a parameter-free $k$-nearest-neighbor ($k$-NN) classifier, our certificate avoids traditional parameter-space complexity measures, KL divergences to a posterior, weight norms, and compression. The bound is tight: trained from scratch, it reaches an 8.0 percentage point gap to test error on CIFAR-10 (ResNet-18) and yields the first non-vacuous certificates we are aware of on CIFAR-100; with frozen DINOv2 representations, it certifies at 1.4\% on CIFAR-10 and 23.1\% on 1,000-class ImageNet. It decomposes additively into three empirical, independently measurable quantities: local class geometry ($k$-NN decoder error), decoder-network agreement, and training stability. This allows the bound to act as a diagnostic tool: we demonstrate that actively destroying local class geometry eliminates generalization while leaving dataset memorization intact, identifying class geometry as a causally relevant mechanism for generalization. Finally, we show that learned representations are significantly less sensitive to weight noise than linear readouts, suggesting why parameter-space certificates often struggle to remain tight.

title: Разработка программного модуля для комплексной оценки качества псевдослучайных последовательностей
abstract: В статье представлена разработка программного модуля для комплексной оценки качества генераторов псевдослучайных чисел (PRNG) с использованием расширенного набора статистических тестов и механизмов параллельной обработки данных. Актуальность работы обусловлена растущими требованиями к надежности криптографических систем в условиях цифровой трансформации и увеличения вычислительной мощности потенциальных злоумышленников. Модуль реализует 31 статистический тест, в том числе 15 тестов NIST STS, 12 тестов Diehard, а также 4 специализированные проверки, и поддерживает три генератора разных классов: Вихрь Мерсенна, CryptMT и криптографически безопасную систему RandomNumberGenerator. Ключевой особенностью решения является параллельное выполнение наборов тестов на основе библиотеки параллелизма задачам и механизма генератора ThreadLocal, что обеспечивает 3–5-кратное ускорение обработки данных на 8-ядерных системах по сравнению с последовательным режимом, гарантируя при этом воспроизводимость результатов для детерминированных генераторов. Модульная трёхуровневая архитектура на платформе C#/.NET 7 позволяет расширять список поддерживаемых генераторов и тестов без изменения ядра системы. В ходе экспериментов генератор Вихрь Мерсенна продемонстрировал скорость генерации 148 миллионов чисел в секунду, пройдя при этом 98% тестов, а потребление оперативной памяти модулем не превышало 650 МБ при обработке выборок объемом до 10 ГБ. Практическая значимость данного решения подтверждается его применимостью к верификации криптографических систем, научным исследованиям и образованию.

title: Relations Acting on Relations: A Layered Conjecture Statement with Definitions, Status and Refutation Conditions
abstract: The research programme asks whether, in systems whose parts are relations, a relation can act on the update rule of another relation, and whether such second-order structure is functionally indispensable. This statement fixes one core claim, an existence claim (C1), defines its terms operationally (intervention-based “effective rule”, functional necessity) and proves it in a toy class by a closed-form comparison: with regime-dependent observation noise, the best state-dependent gain has strictly lower steady-state error than any uniform gain (14–27% in state-estimation error, 1–4% in prediction error for the parameters checked). The toy result did not transfer to the delta-rule engine of the testbed: an oracle regime-dependent scalar gain gave no measurable benefit, and an oracle relation-specific gating gave a structure-dependent but sub-percent benefit. Four further questions are explicitly not part of the core claim and are stated with their status: whether such rules emerge from learning (Q2), reflexive organisation (Q3), a conditional functional candidate for consciousness (Q4), and a heuristic question about non-propagating connection (Q5). The statement gives a status table, refutation conditions, the relation to existing work (metaplasticity, neuromodulated plasticity, fast weights, hypernetworks, adaptive networks) and a list of challenges for readers. Not a proof; not peer reviewed. Companion to doi:10.5281/zenodo.23006539, 23192515, 23373288, 23384438 and 23420727. Proposition 1 is reproduced by the attached script prop1_check.py. AI use: derivations, scripts and drafting were produced with substantial assistance from AI systems; the author is responsible for all content.

title: Mathematicians in the Age of AGI: From Prover to Contemplative Freedom
abstract: README Mathematicians in the Age of AGI: From Prover to Contemplative Freedom This preprint is a working-thought record on the role of mathematicians in the AGI era. It argues that AGI’s cognitive ceiling is geometric, not computational: on the Tarski boundary layer, the tangent and cotangent bundles do not commute, so traversal search fails. The mathematician’s position is not inside the manifold but on the boundary—where projection switching, not search, is the only viable operation. The book has five chapters. Chapter 1 establishes cognitive constraints via the cognitive manifold. Chapter 2 reframes mathematics as mathematical engineering: proofs are cheap, frameworks are not; the mathematician’s output is an interface specification, not a theorem. Chapter 3 identifies three capacities—cross-branch fusion, intuition and inspiration, space and geometry. Chapter 4 defines observing freedom (观自在) as breaking the knowledge obstacle (知见障): seeing the projection itself. Chapter 5 proposes Tian Dao (天道)—respecting the laws of development rather than forcing intervention. The appendices compare these constraints with Baire category theorem and uniform boundedness principle as parallel references. Keywords: AGI; mathematical proof; cognitive manifold; Tarski boundary layer; framework design; observing freedom; Tian Dao; open-source tradition; preprint. License: CC BY 4.0. Knowledge belongs to all humanity.

title: A Cryptographic Abstraction Layer for Integrating NIST Lightweight Cryptography into TLS 1.3
abstract: In the Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) domain, security solutions must remain energy-efficient and reliable under strict latency and real-time requirements, especially for resource-constrained devices.Lightweight Cryptography (LWC) has emerged as a feasible solution to these challenges, offering new cryptographic algorithms developed for IIoT environments.The practical integration of LWC into standardized security protocols remains largely unexplored.In this work, we propose a new Transport Layer Security (TLS) cipher-suites integration that incorporates lightweight cryptographic algorithms, recommended by National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), through a Cryptographic Abstraction Layer (CAL).Measurements on IIoT devices show that the abstraction comes at modest effort: the dispatch cost of CAL peaks at 13.73% for the smallest records and falls to between zero and 9.52% once payloads pass 128 bytes, with most suites under 4%.In return, the layer separates TLS record processing from the cryptographic implementation, conceals cipher internals from the layers above, provides runtime cipher agility, and a fixed memory footprint across the registered suites.The layer drives different ciphers spanning block, sponge, duplex, and stream constructions through one calling convention, confirming that no single internal structure is assumed.
